children.translated_text: <s>Bhartṛhari</s>: <s>Śatakatraya</s> (1. <s>Nītiśataka</s>, 2. <s>Śṛṅgāraśataka</s>, 3. <s>Vairāgyaśataka</s>)
By <s>Bhartṛhari</s>
To that whose form is infinite consciousness alone, unbounded by direction, time, or any other limit,
whose sole measure is one's own direct experience — salutation to that peaceful radiance! || BharSt_1.1 ||
<s>Nīti-śatakam</s> (Century on Wise Conduct)
The learned are consumed by envy,
the powerful are corrupted by pride,
and the rest are afflicted by ignorance —
thus has wise speech grown old upon my body. || BharSt_1.2 ||
An ignorant man is easily won over;
even easier to win over is the true expert.
But one made falsely clever by a mere scrap of knowledge —

children.text: brahmāpi taṃ naraṃ na rañjayati || BharSt_1.3 ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Brahmā</s> himself cannot please such a person. || BharSt_1.3 ||
One might forcibly extract a jewel from between the fangs of a crocodile's mouth,
one might even cross the ocean turbulent with rolling garlands of waves,

children.text: bhujaṅgam api kopitaṃ śirasi puṣpavad dhārayet
children.translated_text: one might wear an enraged serpent upon one's head as though it were a flower —
but one can never win over the mind of a stubborn fool. || BharSt_1.4 ||

children.text: labheta sikatāsu tailam api yatnataḥ pīḍayan
children.translated_text: One might, by pressing hard, obtain oil even from sand,
one tormented by thirst might drink water even from a mirage,
one might, wandering somewhere, chance upon the horn of a hare —
but one can never win over the mind of a stubborn fool. || BharSt_1.5 ||
He strains to bind a mighty serpent with tender lotus-stalk fibers,
he girds himself to cut a diamond with the edge of a <s>śirīṣa</s> (silk-cotton) blossom,
he endeavors to sweeten the salt ocean with a single drop of honey —

children.text: netuṃ vāñchanti yaḥ khalān pathi satāṃ sūktaiḥ sudhā-syandibhiḥ || BharSt_1.6 ||
children.translated_text: he who wishes to lead the wicked onto the path of the virtuous with nectar-flowing wise sayings. || BharSt_1.6 ||
Self-possessed, of singular virtue, fashioned by the Creator
as a covering for ignorance —
especially in the assembly of the learned,
silence is the ornament of the unwise. || BharSt_1.7 ||

children.text: yadā kiñcij-jño 'haṃ dvipa iva madāndhaḥ samabhavaṃ
tadā sarvajño 'smīty abhavad avaliptaṃ mama manaḥ
children.translated_text: then my mind grew haughty, thinking 'I am omniscient!'
But when, bit by bit, I learned something in the company of the wise,

children.text: tadā mūrkho 'smīti jvara iva mado me vyapagataḥ || BharSt_1.8 ||
children.translated_text: then my pride departed like a fever, and I realized 'I am a fool!' || BharSt_1.8 ||
When I knew but little, I became blind with arrogance like a rutting elephant;
Gnawing with relish at a fleshless human bone, full of worm-holes, smeared with saliva, foul-smelling and disgusting,
finding in it an incomparable flavor,

children.text: surapatim api śvā pārśvasthaṃ vilokya na śaṅkate
children.translated_text: a dog does not flinch even when <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, stands beside him —

children.text: na hi gaṇayati kṣudro jantuḥ parigraha-phalgutām || BharSt_1.9 ||
children.translated_text: for a base creature never considers the pettiness of its possessions. || BharSt_1.9 ||
From heaven to <s>Śarva</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) head, from <s>Paśupati</s>'s head to the mountain,

children.text: mhīdhrād uttuṅgād avanim avaneś cāpi jaladhim |
children.translated_text: from the lofty mountain to the earth, and from the earth to the ocean —
ever downward has the <s>Gaṅgā</s> descended, step by step;
indeed, the fall of those who have lost discernment is a hundredfold. || BharSt_1.10 ||

children.text: śakyo vārayituṃ jalena hutabhuk cchatreṇa sūryātapo
children.translated_text: Fire can be quenched with water, the sun's heat warded off with a parasol,
a mighty elephant controlled with a sharp goad, an ox or donkey with a stick,

children.text: vyādhir bheṣaja-saṅgrahaiś ca vividhair mantra-prayogair viṣaṃ
children.translated_text: disease by various collections of remedies, and poison by the application of <s>mantras</s> —

children.text: sarvasyauṣadham asti śāstra-vihitaṃ mūrkhasya nasty auṣadhim || BharSt_1.11 ||
children.translated_text: for everything there exists a cure prescribed by the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures), but for a fool there is no remedy. || BharSt_1.11 ||
One who is devoid of literature, music, and art
is verily a beast, only lacking a tail and horns.
Though he lives without eating grass,
that is indeed the supreme good fortune of cattle. || BharSt_1.12 ||

children.text: yeṣāṃ na vidyā na tapo na dānaṃ
children.translated_text: Those who possess neither learning, nor austerity, nor charity,

children.text: jñānaṃ na śīlaṃ na guṇo na dharmaḥ |
children.translated_text: nor wisdom, nor good conduct, nor virtue, nor <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) —
they are a burden upon the earth in the mortal world,
they wander as beasts in human form. || BharSt_1.13 ||
among the forest-dwelling creatures,
than to keep the company of fools
even in the palaces of <s>Indra</s>. || BharSt_1.14 ||
Better to have wandered in mountain fastnesses
Poets whose speech is made beautiful by the refinement of <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), whose teachings are worthy of being imparted to students,

children.text: vikhyātāḥ kavayo vasanti viṣaye yasya prabhor nirdhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: who are renowned — they dwell impoverished in the domain of such a lord.

children.text: taj-jāḍyaṃ vasudhādipasya kavayas tv arthaṃ vināpīśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: That is the stupidity of the ruler of the earth; the poets, however, are lords even without wealth —

children.text: kutsyāḥ syuḥ kuparīkṣakā hi maṇayo yair arghataḥ pātitāḥ || BharSt_1.15 ||
children.translated_text: it is the poor appraisers who are to be blamed, those by whom gems are reduced in value. || BharSt_1.15 ||

children.text: hartur yāti na gocaraṃ kim api śaṃ puṣṇāti yat sarvadā 'py
children.translated_text: It does not come within the reach of a thief, it always nourishes some inexplicable good,

children.text: arthibhyaḥ pratipādyamānam aniśaṃ prāpnoti vṛddhiṃ parām |
children.translated_text: though constantly given away to supplicants, it attains the highest increase,

children.text: kalpānteṣv api na prayāti nidhanaṃ vidyākhyam antardhanaṃ
children.translated_text: even at the end of a cosmic age it does not perish — this hidden treasure called knowledge.

children.text: yeṣāṃ tān prati mānam ujjhata nṛpāḥ kas taiḥ saha spardhate || BharSt_1.16 ||
children.translated_text: O kings, abandon your pride toward those who possess it; who can compete with them? || BharSt_1.16 ||
Do not look down upon the learned who have attained the highest truth —

children.text: tṛṇam iva laghu lakṣmīr naiva tān saṃruṇaddhi |
children.translated_text: wealth, light as a blade of grass, can never obstruct them.
For those whose temples are darkened by fresh streaks of rut-fluid,

children.text: na bhavati bisatantur vāraṇaṃ vāraṇānām || BharSt_1.17 ||
children.translated_text: a lotus-stalk fiber is no barrier for mighty elephants. || BharSt_1.17 ||
Even if an angered Creator destroys the swan's delight in sporting among lotus groves,
the sport among lotus-filled lakes is entirely destroyed by an enraged Providence,
he is nonetheless unable to take away that celebrated skill
of discerning milk from water, the swan's renowned wisdom. || BharSt_1.18 ||

children.text: keyūrāṇi na bhūṣayanti puruṣaṃ hārā na candrojjvalā
children.translated_text: Armbands do not adorn a man, nor necklaces brilliant as the moon,

children.text: na snānaṃ na vilepanaṃ na kusumaṃ nālaṅkṛtā mūrdhajāḥ |
children.translated_text: nor bathing, nor unguents, nor flowers, nor decorated hair —

children.text: vāṇy ekā samalaṅkaroti puruṣaṃ yā saṃskṛtā dhāryate
children.translated_text: speech alone adorns a man, speech that is cultivated and maintained;

children.text: kṣīyante khalu bhūṣaṇāni satataṃ vāg-bhūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇam || BharSt_1.19 ||
children.translated_text: all other ornaments perish — the ornament of speech is the true ornament. || BharSt_1.19 ||

children.text: vidyā nāma narasya rūpam adhikaṃ pracchanna-guptaṃ dhanaṃ
children.translated_text: Learning is man's supreme form, it is wealth hidden and well-guarded,

children.text: vidyā bhogakarī yaśaḥ-sukhakarī vidyā gurūṇāṃ guruḥ |
children.translated_text: learning bestows enjoyment, brings fame and happiness; learning is the teacher of teachers,

children.text: vidyā bandhujano videśa-gamane vidyā parā devatā
children.translated_text: learning is one's kinsman when traveling abroad, learning is the supreme deity —

children.text: vidyā rājasu pūjyate na tu dhanaṃ vidyā-vihīnaḥ paśuḥ || BharSt_1.20 ||
children.translated_text: learning is honored among kings, not mere wealth; one without learning is a beast. || BharSt_1.20 ||

children.text: kṣāntiś cet kavacena kiṃ kim aribhiḥ krodho 'sti ced dehināṃ
children.translated_text: If one has forbearance, what need of armor? If beings possess anger, what need of enemies?

children.text: jñātiś ced analena kiṃ yadi suhṛd divyauṣadhaṃ kiṃ phalam |
children.translated_text: If one has a kinsman, what need of fire? If one has a good friend, what need of divine medicines?

children.text: kiṃ sarpair yadi durjanāḥ kim u dhanair vidyā 'navadyā yadi
children.translated_text: If there are wicked men, what need of serpents? If one has blameless learning, what need of wealth?

children.text: vrīḍā cet kim u bhūṣaṇaiḥ sukavitā yady asti rājyena kim || BharSt_1.21 ||
children.translated_text: If there is modesty, what need of ornaments? If there is fine poetry, what need of a kingdom? || BharSt_1.21 ||

children.text: dākṣiṇyaṃ svajane dayā parijane śāṭhyaṃ sadā durjane
children.translated_text: Courtesy toward one's own people, compassion toward dependents, cunning toward the wicked,

children.text: prītiḥ sādhujane nayo nṛpa-jane vidvaj-jane cārjavam |
children.translated_text: affection toward the virtuous, statesmanship toward rulers, and straightforwardness toward the learned,

children.text: śauryaṃ śatru-jane kṣamā guru-jane kāntā-jane dhṛṣṭatā
children.translated_text: valor toward enemies, patience toward elders, boldness toward women —

children.text: ye caivaṃ puruṣāḥ kalāsu kuśalās teṣv eva loka-sthitiḥ || BharSt_1.22 ||
children.translated_text: those men who are skilled in these arts, upon them alone the world rests. || BharSt_1.22 ||

children.text: jāḍyaṃ dhiyo harati siñcati vāci satyaṃ
children.translated_text: It removes the dullness of the intellect, sprinkles truth upon one's speech,
it bestows elevation of honor and dispels sin,
it gladdens the heart and spreads fame in all directions —

children.text: sat-saṅgatiḥ kathaya kiṃ na karoti puṃsām || BharSt_1.23 ||
children.translated_text: the company of the good — tell me, what does it not do for a man? || BharSt_1.23 ||
Victorious are those fortunate ones,
those lords among poets who have attained perfection of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) —
for in their body of fame there is
no fear born of old age and death. || BharSt_1.24 ||

children.text: sūnuḥ sac-caritaḥ satī priyatamā svāmī prasādonmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: A son of good conduct, a faithful beloved wife, a master inclined to grace,

children.text: snigdhaṃ mitram avañcakaḥ parijano niḥkleśa-leśaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: an affectionate friend, honest servants, and a mind free from the slightest affliction,

children.text: ākāro ruciraḥ sthiraś ca vibhavo vidyāvadātaṃ mukhaṃ
children.translated_text: a handsome form, steadfast wealth, a face radiant with learning —

children.text: tuṣṭe viṣṭapa-kaṣṭa-hāriṇi harau samprāpyate dehinā || BharSt_1.25 ||
children.translated_text: all these are obtained by an embodied soul when <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the remover of the world's sorrows, is pleased. || BharSt_1.25 ||
Abstaining from taking life, restraint from seizing another's wealth, truthful speech,
timely giving according to one's ability, silence regarding the affairs of other men's women,

children.text: tṛṣṇā-sroto vibhaṅgo guruṣu ca vinayaḥ sarva-bhūtānukampā
children.translated_text: breaking the current of craving, humility toward teachers, compassion toward all beings —

children.text: sāmānyaḥ sarva-śāstreṣv anupahata-vidhiḥ śreyasām eṣa panthāḥ || BharSt_1.26 ||
children.translated_text: this is the common, unimpaired way to blessedness prescribed in all <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures). || BharSt_1.26 ||
The base do not even begin an undertaking out of fear of obstacles;
the mediocre begin but give up when struck down by obstacles.
Even when struck down by obstacles again and again,
the noble never abandon what they have begun. || BharSt_1.27 ||

children.text: asanto nābhyarthyāḥ suhṛd api na yācyaḥ kṛśa-dhanaḥ
children.translated_text: The unworthy should not be entreated, nor should a friend be begged from when his means are slender;

children.text: priyā nyāyyā vṛttir malinam asubhaṅge 'py asukaram |
children.translated_text: one's livelihood should be fair and just — even when life is at stake, dishonorable conduct is unacceptable.

children.text: vipady uccaiḥ stheyaṃ padam anuvidheyaṃ ca mahatāṃ
children.translated_text: In adversity one must stand tall, and one must follow the path of the great —

children.text: satāṃ kenoddiṣṭaṃ viṣamam asidhārā-vratam idam || BharSt_1.28 ||
children.translated_text: who has ordained this arduous vow, sharp as a sword's edge, for the virtuous? || BharSt_1.28 ||
Though starving with hunger, though emaciated by old age, though his breath is feeble, though he has fallen into the direst state,

children.text: āpanno 'pi vipanna-dīdhitir iti prāṇeṣu naśyatsv api |
children.translated_text: though his luster has faded and his very life-breaths are ebbing away —
with his desire fixed solely on devouring the flesh of the frontal globe of a mighty rutting elephant,

children.text: kiṃ jīrṇaṃ tṛṇam atti māna-mahatām agresaraḥ kesarī || BharSt_1.29 ||
children.translated_text: does the lion, foremost among the proud, ever eat withered grass? || BharSt_1.29 ||
A dog, having obtained a meatless, dirty bone of a cow, with only a few sinews and scraps of fat remaining,

children.text: śvā labdhvā paritoṣam eti na tu tat tasya kṣudhā-śāntaye |
children.translated_text: is content, yet even that does not appease his hunger.

children.text: siṃho jambukam aṅkam āgatam api tyaktvā nihanti dvipaṃ
children.translated_text: A lion, however, spurning a jackal that has come within reach, slays an elephant instead —

children.text: sarvaḥ kṛcchra-gato 'pi vāñchanti janaḥ sattvānurūpaṃ phalam || BharSt_1.30 ||
children.translated_text: everyone, even in dire straits, desires fruit befitting their nature. || BharSt_1.30 ||
Wagging its tail, falling down at another's feet,
throwing itself on the ground, displaying its belly and mouth —
this a dog does for one who gives it a morsel; but a lordly elephant

children.text: dhīraṃ vilokayati cāṭu-śataiś ca bhuṅkte || BharSt_1.31 ||
children.translated_text: gazes calmly and eats only after being coaxed with a hundred flatteries. || BharSt_1.31 ||
In this revolving cycle of existence,
who that has died is not born again?
Truly born is only the one by whose birth
the family line rises to eminence. || BharSt_1.32 ||
Like a cluster of flowers,
twofold is the course of the noble-minded:
either upon the head of all the world,
or withering away in the forest. || BharSt_1.33 ||
There are other luminaries, five or six, worthy of esteem, such as <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and the rest;

children.text: tān praty eṣa viśeṣa-vikrama-rucī rāhur na vairāyate |
children.translated_text: toward them <s>Rāhu</s>, delighting in extraordinary valor, shows no enmity.
He swallows only the two — the lords of day and night, the two luminaries, the sun and moon —

children.text: bhrātaḥ parvaṇi paśya dānava-patiḥ śīrṣāvaśeṣākṛtiḥ || BharSt_1.34 ||
children.translated_text: Brother, behold at the eclipse: this lord of <s>Dānavas</s> (demons), whose body is but a severed head! || BharSt_1.34 ||
<s>Śeṣa</s> bears the multitude of worlds placed upon the flat of his hoods,

children.text: kamaṭha-patinā madhye-pṛṣṭhaṃ sadā sa ca dhāryate |
children.translated_text: and he in turn is always borne upon the middle of the back of the lord of tortoises.

children.text: tam api kurute kroḍādhīnaṃ payodhir anādarād
children.translated_text: Even him the ocean supports without effort upon its breast —
ah, boundless indeed are the glorious deeds of the great! || BharSt_1.35 ||
Better that his wings be shattered by the blows of the thunderbolt hurled by the wrathful <s>Indra</s>,
heavy with the erupting billows of abundant flame,
alas, while his father, the son of the snowy mountain, is helpless in distress —

children.text: na cāsau sampātaḥ payasi payasāṃ patyur ucitaḥ || BharSt_1.36 ||
children.translated_text: than that descent into the waters of the lord of waters be fitting for <s>Maināka</s>. || BharSt_1.36 ||
Even a lion cub pounces
upon elephants whose temple-walls are stained with rut-fluid.
Such is the nature of the courageous —

children.text: na khalu vayas tejaso hetuḥ || BharSt_1.37 ||
children.translated_text: age is certainly not the cause of valor. || BharSt_1.37 ||

children.text: jātir yātu rasātalaṃ guṇa-gaṇais tatrāpy adho gamyatāṃ
children.translated_text: Let birth go to the nether world, let clusters of virtues go even further below,

children.text: śīlaṃ śaila-taṭāt patatv abhijanaḥ sandahyatāṃ vahninā |
children.translated_text: let good character fall from a mountain cliff, let noble lineage be consumed by fire,

children.text: śaurye vairiṇi vajram āśu nipatatv artho 'stu naḥ kevalaṃ
children.translated_text: let a thunderbolt swiftly fall upon valor — just let us have wealth alone,

children.text: yenaikena vinā guṇas tṛṇa-lava-prāyāḥ samastā ime || BharSt_1.38 ||
children.translated_text: without which alone all these virtues are worthless as a scrap of grass. || BharSt_1.38 ||
Earn wealth, O scion of <s>Kakutstha</s>!
This world is rooted in wealth.
I perceive no difference
between a pauper and a dead man. || BharSt_1.39 ||
The same unimpaired senses, the same name,

children.text: sā buddhir apratihatā vacanaṃ tad eva |
children.translated_text: the same unobstructed intellect, the same speech —
yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth, in an instant,

children.text: so 'py anya eva bhavatīti vicitram etat || BharSt_1.40 ||
children.translated_text: becomes as if an entirely different person — how wondrous this is! || BharSt_1.40 ||
He who has wealth — that man is noble-born,
he is learned, he is well-versed in scripture, a knower of virtues,

children.text: sa eva vaktā sa ca darśanīyaḥ
children.translated_text: he alone is eloquent, he alone is handsome —
all virtues take refuge in gold. || BharSt_1.41 ||

children.text: daurmantryān nṛpatir vinaśyati yatiḥ saṅgāt suto lālanāt
children.translated_text: A king perishes through bad counsel, an ascetic through attachment, a son through pampering,
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> through neglect of study, a family through a wicked son, good character through serving the base,

children.text: hrīr madyād anavekṣaṇād api kṛṣiḥ snehaḥ pravāsāśrayān
children.translated_text: modesty through wine, agriculture through inattention, love through prolonged absence,

children.text: maitrī cāpraṇayāt samṛddhir anayāt tyāga-pramādād dhanam || BharSt_1.42 ||
children.translated_text: friendship through lack of affection, prosperity through misconduct, and wealth through carelessness in giving. || BharSt_1.42 ||
Giving, enjoyment, and destruction — these three
are the destinies of wealth.
He who neither gives nor enjoys,
for him there is a third fate (ruin). || BharSt_1.43 ||
A gem polished on the whetstone, a weapon scarred by victory in battle,
an elephant wasted by rut, rivers with shrunken sandbars in autumn,
the moon reduced to a sliver, a young wife exhausted by love —

children.text: tan-nimnā śobhante galita-vibhavāś cārthiṣu narāḥ || BharSt_1.44 ||
children.translated_text: even so, those who have lost their wealth shine all the more when they give to supplicants. || BharSt_1.44 ||
A certain man, when impoverished, craves even a handful of barley;

children.text: sa paścāt sampūrṇaḥ kalayati dharitrīṃ tṛṇa-samām |
children.translated_text: that same man, once prosperous again, regards the whole earth as a blade of grass.
Therefore, because of the inconstancy of greatness and smallness in the fortunes of the wealthy,

children.text: avasthā vastūni prathayati ca saṅkocayati ca || BharSt_1.45 ||
children.translated_text: circumstance both magnifies and diminishes things. || BharSt_1.45 ||

children.text: tenādya vatsam iva lokam amuṃ puṣāṇa
children.translated_text: then nourish this people like her calf;
and when that calf is properly and constantly nourished,
the earth yields various fruits like a <s>kalpalatā</s> (wish-fulfilling vine). || BharSt_1.46 ||
O King, if you wish to milk this earth-cow,
Both truthful and false, both harsh and sweet-spoken,
both cruel and compassionate, both greedy and generous,
ever-spending yet ever-replenishing its abundant treasury —
royal policy is multiform, like a courtesan. || BharSt_1.47 ||
generosity, enjoyment, and safeguarding of friends —
for those in whom these six virtues are not active,
what use is the patronage of a king? || BharSt_1.48 ||
Command, fame, protection of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: yad dhātrā nija-bhāla-paṭṭa-likhitaṃ stokaṃ mahad vā dhanaṃ
children.translated_text: Whatever wealth, small or great, the Creator has inscribed on one's forehead,

children.text: tat prāpnoti marusthale 'pi nitarāṃ merau tato nādhikam |
children.translated_text: that much one obtains even in a desert — and no more even on Mount <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: tad dhīro bhava vittavatsu kṛpaṇāṃ vṛttiṃ vṛthā sā kṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore be resolute, O wise one; do not adopt a wretched manner toward the wealthy in vain —

children.text: kūpe paśya payonidhāv api ghaṭo gṛhṇāti tulyaṃ jalam || BharSt_1.49 ||
children.translated_text: look, whether from a well or from the ocean, a pot takes only the same measure of water. || BharSt_1.49 ||
"You alone are the sustainer of the <s>cātaka</s> (rain-bird)" —
to whom is this not evident?
O noble cloud, why do you wait
for our piteous entreaty? || BharSt_1.50 ||

children.text: re re cātaka sāvadhāna-manasā mitra kṣaṇaṃ śrūyatām
children.translated_text: O, O <s>cātaka</s>, my friend, listen attentively for a moment:

children.text: ambhodā bahavo vasanti gagane sarve 'pi naitādṛśāḥ |
children.translated_text: many clouds dwell in the sky, but not all are alike.

children.text: kecid vṛṣṭibhir ārdrayanti vasudhāṃ garjanti kecid vṛthā
children.translated_text: Some drench the earth with rain, others merely thunder in vain —

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ paśyasi tasya tasya purato mā brūhi dīnaṃ vacaḥ || BharSt_1.51 ||
children.translated_text: do not utter humble words before every one you see. || BharSt_1.51 ||
Cruelty, quarreling without cause,
coveting another's wealth and another's wife,
intolerance toward the good and toward kinsmen —
this is the innate nature of the wicked. || BharSt_1.52 ||
A wicked person should be avoided
even if adorned with learning;
is a serpent decorated with a jewel
any less frightening? || BharSt_1.53 ||

children.text: jāḍyaṃ hrīmati gaṇyate vrata-rucau dambhaḥ śucau kaitavaṃ
children.translated_text: In the modest, stupidity is imputed; in the devout, hypocrisy; in the pure, deceit;

children.text: śūre nirghṛṇatā munau vimatitā dainyaṃ priyālāpini |
children.translated_text: in the brave, mercilessness; in the sage, folly; in the sweet-spoken, servility;

children.text: tejasviny avaliptatā mukharatā vaktary aśaktiḥ sthire
children.translated_text: in the spirited, arrogance; in the eloquent, garrulity; in the steadfast, incapacity —

children.text: tat ko nāma guṇo bhavet sa guṇināṃ yo durjanair nāṅkitaḥ || BharSt_1.54 ||
children.translated_text: what virtue, then, could exist in the virtuous that the wicked would not brand as a flaw? || BharSt_1.54 ||

children.text: lobhaś ced aguṇena kiṃ piśunatā yady asti kiṃ pātakaiḥ
children.translated_text: If greed is present, what need of other vices? If slander is there, what need of other sins?

children.text: satyaṃ cet tapasā ca kiṃ śuci mano yady asti tīrthena kim |
children.translated_text: If truth is present, what need of austerity? If the mind is pure, what need of pilgrimage?

children.text: saujanyaṃ yadi kiṃ guṇaiḥ sumahimā yady asti kiṃ maṇḍanaiḥ
children.translated_text: If there is nobility, what need of other virtues? If there is great glory, what need of ornaments?

children.text: sad-vidyā yadi kiṃ dhanair apayaśo yady asti kiṃ mṛtyunā || BharSt_1.55 ||
children.translated_text: If there is true learning, what need of wealth? If there is infamy, what need of death? || BharSt_1.55 ||
The moon pale by day, a woman whose youth has faded,
a lake bereft of lotuses, a face without learning in its features,
a lord devoted only to wealth, a good man perpetually destitute,

children.text: nṛpāṅgaṇa-gataḥ khalo manasi sapta śalyāni me || BharSt_1.56 ||
children.translated_text: a villain ensconced in the royal court — these are seven thorns in my heart. || BharSt_1.56 ||
No one is truly a kinsman
of kings given to fierce anger;
fire burns even the priest
who is pouring oblations into it. || BharSt_1.57 ||
If silent, he is a mute; if skilled in discourse, a chatterbox or a babbler;

children.text: dhṛṣṭaḥ pārśve vasati ca sadā dūrataś cāpragalbhaḥ |
children.translated_text: if he stays near, he is presumptuous; if at a distance, he lacks confidence;

children.text: kṣāntyā bhīrur yadi na sahate prāyaśo nābhijātaḥ
children.translated_text: if patient, he is a coward; if he does not endure, he is of low birth —

children.text: sevādharmaḥ parama-gahano yoginām apy agamyaḥ || BharSt_1.58 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> (code) of service is supremely inscrutable, unfathomable even to <s>yogins</s>. || BharSt_1.58 ||
When one who has made all villainy manifest, who is utterly unbridled,
whose base conduct has spread far and wide from its very inception,
who, by mere fate, has obtained prosperity, who hates virtue —
when such a wretch holds sway, happiness is attained only by those who fall within his orbit. || BharSt_1.59 ||
Grand at the beginning, diminishing by degrees;
slight at first, then increasing over time —
divided like the morning and afternoon shadows of a day,
such is the friendship of the base and the noble, respectively. || BharSt_1.60 ||
Deer, fish, and good men — whose livelihood depends on grass, water, and contentment —
for them, hunters, fishermen, and slanderers are enemies without cause in this world. || BharSt_1.61 ||

children.text: vāñchā sajjana-saṅgame para-guṇe prītir gurau namratā
children.translated_text: Desire for the company of the good, delight in others' virtues, humility before the teacher,

children.text: vidyāyāṃ vyasanaṃ sva-yoṣiti ratir lokāpavādād bhayam |
children.translated_text: passion for learning, devotion to one's own wife, fear of public censure,

children.text: bhaktiḥ śūlini śaktir ātma-damane saṃsarga-muktiḥ khale
children.translated_text: devotion to <s>Śūlin</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), strength in self-restraint, freedom from association with the base —

children.text: yeṣv ete nivasanti nirmala-guṇās tebhyo narebhyo namaḥ || BharSt_1.62 ||
children.translated_text: to those men in whom these pure virtues dwell, I bow. || BharSt_1.62 ||
Fortitude in adversity, forbearance in prosperity,
eloquence in the assembly, valor in battle,
zeal for fame, devotion to learning —
this is the innate nature of great souls. || BharSt_1.63 ||
Giving in secret, elaborate hospitality to one who arrives at the house,

children.text: priyaṃ kṛtvā maunaṃ sadasi kathanaṃ cāpy upakṛteḥ |
children.translated_text: silence after doing a kindness, yet public acknowledgment of favors received,
no pride in wealth, not a trace of disparaging talk about others —

children.text: satāṃ kenoddiṣṭaṃ viṣamam asidhārā-vratam idam || BharSt_1.64 ||
children.translated_text: who ordained this arduous razor's-edge vow for the virtuous? || BharSt_1.64 ||
Praiseworthy generosity in the hand, the head bowed in devotion at the <s>guru's</s> feet,

children.text: mukhe satyā vāṇī vijayi bhujayor vīryam atulam |
children.translated_text: truthful speech on the lips, matchless victorious valor in the arms,

children.text: hṛdi svacchā vṛttiḥ śrutim adhigataṃ ca śravaṇayor
children.translated_text: a pure disposition in the heart, and sacred learning received by the ears —

children.text: vināpy aiśvaryeṇa prakṛti-mahatāṃ maṇḍanam idam || BharSt_1.65 ||
children.translated_text: even without sovereignty, this is the adornment of the naturally great. || BharSt_1.65 ||

children.text:
sampatsu mahatāṃ cittaṃ
bhavaty utpala-komalam |āpatsu ca mahāśailaśilā-

children.translated_text: as a mass of mountain rock. || BharSt_1.66 ||
In prosperity, the mind of the great becomes as soft as a lotus petal; in adversity, it becomes as hard

children.text: santaptāyasi saṃsthitasya payaso nāmāpi na jñāyate
children.translated_text: Of water resting on heated iron, not even the name remains;
that same water, resting on a lotus leaf, gleams like a pearl;
fallen into the heart of an ocean-shell under the <s>Svāti</s> star, it becomes a genuine pearl —
generally, the quality of inferior, middling, or superior arises from one's associations. || BharSt_1.67 ||

children.text: prīṇāti yaḥ sucaritaiḥ pitaraṃ sa putro
children.translated_text: He is a true son who pleases his father by good conduct;

children.text: yad bhartur eva hitam icchati tat kalatram |
children.translated_text: she is a true wife who desires only her husband's welfare;

children.text: tan mitram āpadi sukhe ca sama-kriyaṃ yad
children.translated_text: that is a true friend who acts alike in adversity and in joy —

children.text: etat trayaṃ jagati puṇya-kṛto labhante || BharSt_1.68 ||
children.translated_text: only the meritorious obtain these three in this world. || BharSt_1.68 ||

children.text: eko devaḥ keśavo vā śivo vā
children.translated_text: One God — be it <s>Keśava</s> or <s>Śiva</s>;

children.text: hy ekaṃ mitraṃ bhūpatir vā yatir vā |
children.translated_text: one friend — be it a king or an ascetic;

children.text: eko vāsaḥ pattane vā vane vā
children.translated_text: one dwelling — be it in a city or in a forest;

children.text: hy ekā bhāryā sundarī vā darī vā || BharSt_1.69 ||
children.translated_text: one wife — be she a beauty or a cave (of solitude). || BharSt_1.69 ||
Rising high through humility, making their own virtues known by praising others' merits,
accomplishing their own purposes through vast and generous efforts undertaken for others' sake,
silencing the harsh and abusive words of the wicked by patience alone —

children.text: santaḥ sāścarya-caryā jagati bahu-matāḥ kasya nābhyarcanīyāḥ || BharSt_1.70 ||
children.translated_text: the good, whose conduct inspires wonder, are honored by all the world. Who would not revere them? || BharSt_1.70 ||
Trees bow low when laden with fruit;
clouds hang near the earth when heavy with fresh water;
noble persons remain unassuming amid prosperity —
such is the nature of those devoted to helping others. || BharSt_1.71 ||
The ear is adorned by sacred learning, not by earrings;
the hand is adorned by giving, not by bracelets;
the body of the compassionate shines
through acts of benevolence, not through sandalwood paste. || BharSt_1.72 ||
He restrains one from sin, directs one toward the good,
conceals one's secrets, makes one's virtues known,

children.text: āpad-gataṃ ca na jahāti dadāti kāle
children.translated_text: does not abandon one in calamity, and gives in time of need —
the wise declare these to be the marks of a true friend. || BharSt_1.73 ||
The sun causes the lotus pond to bloom;
the moon delights the cluster of night-lilies;
the rain cloud gives water even unasked —
the good are naturally dedicated to the welfare of others. || BharSt_1.74 ||

children.text: eke sat-puruṣāḥ parārtha-ghaṭakāḥ svārthaṃ parityajanti ye
children.translated_text: Some noble persons, devoted to others' welfare, abandon their own interests entirely;

children.text: sāmānyās tu parārtham udyama-bhṛtaḥ svārthāvirodhena ye |
children.translated_text: ordinary people exert themselves for others only when it does not conflict with self-interest;

children.text: te 'mī mānuṣa-rākṣasāḥ parahitaṃ svārthāya nighnanti ye
children.translated_text: those human-demons destroy others' welfare for their own gain —

children.text: ye tu ghnanti nirarthakaṃ parahitaṃ te ke na jānīmahe || BharSt_1.75 ||
children.translated_text: but those who destroy others' good for no reason at all, what are they? We cannot say. || BharSt_1.75 ||

children.text: kṣīreṇātmagatodakāya hi guṇā dattā purā te 'khilā
children.translated_text: Milk once gave all its virtues to the water that had entered it;

children.text: kṣīrottāpam avekṣya tena payasā svātmā kṛśānau hutaḥ |
children.translated_text: seeing the milk being scalded, that water cast itself into the fire;

children.text: gantuṃ pāvakam unmanas tad abhavad dṛṣṭvā tu mitrāpadaṃ
children.translated_text: the milk, anxious to follow its friend into the flames, seeing its friend's distress —

children.text: yuktaṃ tena jalena śāmyati satāṃ maitrī punas tv īdṛśī || BharSt_1.76 ||
children.translated_text: was then united with that water and cooled. Such indeed is the friendship of the good. || BharSt_1.76 ||

children.text: itaḥ svapiti keśavaḥ kulam itas tadīya-dviṣām
children.translated_text: On this side sleeps <s>Keśava</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>); on that side, the clan of his enemies;

children.text: itaś ca śaraṇārthināṃ śikhariṇāṃ gaṇāḥ śerate |
children.translated_text: on another side, the hosts of mountains seeking refuge lie at rest;
here too rests the submarine fire along with all the world-destroying forces —

children.text: aho vitatam ūrjitaṃ bhara-sahaṃ sindhor vapuḥ || BharSt_1.77 ||
children.translated_text: ah, how vast, mighty, and burden-bearing is the body of the Ocean! || BharSt_1.77 ||

children.text: tṛṣṇāṃ chindhi bhaja kṣamāṃ jahi madaṃ pāpe ratiṃ mā kṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: Sever craving, embrace forbearance, renounce pride, take no delight in sin,

children.text: satyaṃ brūhy anuyāhi sādhu-padavīṃ sevasva vidvaj-janam |
children.translated_text: speak the truth, follow the path of the righteous, serve the learned,

children.text: mānyān mānaya vidviṣo 'py anunaya prakhyāpaya praśrayaṃ
children.translated_text: honor the honorable, conciliate even enemies, proclaim your humility,

children.text: kīrtiṃ pālaya duḥkhite kuru dayām etat satāṃ ceṣṭitam || BharSt_1.78 ||
children.translated_text: preserve your fame, show compassion to the afflicted — this is the conduct of the good. || BharSt_1.78 ||
Filled with the nectar of merit in mind, speech, and body,
gladdening the three worlds with streams of benevolence,
magnifying even the smallest atoms of others' virtues into mountains,

children.text: nija-hṛdi vikasantaḥ santa santaḥ kiyantaḥ || BharSt_1.79 ||
children.translated_text: and blossoming ever in their own hearts — how few are such good souls, truly good! || BharSt_1.79 ||
What use is a mountain of gold or a mountain of silver

children.text: yatrāśritāś ca taravas taravas ta eva |
children.translated_text: where the trees sheltered upon it remain just ordinary trees?
We esteem <s>Malaya</s> (the Sandalwood Mountain) alone, by whose nurturing
even the <s>kaṅkola</s>, <s>nimba</s> (neem), and <s>kaṭuja</s> trees become fragrant as sandalwood. || BharSt_1.80 ||
The gods were not satisfied by costly gems,
nor did they succumb to fear from the dreadful poison;
without obtaining the nectar, they would not cease —
the resolute do not desist from their determined goal. || BharSt_1.81 ||

children.text: kvacit pṛthvīśayyaḥ kvacid api ca paraṅka-śayanaḥ
children.translated_text: Sometimes sleeping on the bare ground, sometimes resting on a fine couch,

children.text: kvacic chākāhāraḥ kvacid api ca śālyodana-ruciḥ |
children.translated_text: sometimes eating only vegetables, sometimes relishing rice and delicacies,

children.text: kvacit kanthādhārī kvacid api ca divyāmbaradharo
children.translated_text: sometimes wearing a patched garment, sometimes clad in divine robes —

children.text: manasvī kāryārthī na gaṇayati duḥkhaṃ na ca sukham || BharSt_1.82 ||
children.translated_text: the man of resolve, intent on his purpose, heeds neither sorrow nor pleasure. || BharSt_1.82 ||
The ornament of sovereignty is noble character; the ornament of valor is restraint of speech;

children.text: jñānasyopaśamaḥ śrutasya vinayo vittasya pātre vyayaḥ |
children.translated_text: the ornament of knowledge is tranquility; the ornament of learning is modesty; the ornament of wealth is giving to the worthy;

children.text: akrodhas tapasaḥ kṣamā prabhavitur dharmasya nirvājatā
children.translated_text: the ornament of austerity is freedom from anger; the ornament of the powerful is forbearance; the ornament of <s>dharma</s> is freedom from deceit —

children.text: sarveṣām api sarva-kāraṇam idaṃ śīlaṃ paraṃ bhūṣaṇam || BharSt_1.83 ||
children.translated_text: and the supreme ornament underlying all these is good conduct. || BharSt_1.83 ||
Let the experts in statecraft blame or praise,
let <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) come or go as she pleases,

children.text: adyaiva vā maraṇam astu yugāntare vā
children.translated_text: let death come today or at the end of an age —

children.text: nyāyyāt pathaḥ pravicalanti padaṃ na dhīrāḥ || BharSt_1.84 ||
children.translated_text: the resolute do not deviate a single step from the righteous path. || BharSt_1.84 ||
A mouse, its hopes dashed, its body curled up in a basket, its senses dulled by hunger,

children.text: kṛtvākhur vivaraṃ svayaṃ nipatito naktaṃ mukhe bhoginaḥ |
children.translated_text: having gnawed a hole, fell of its own accord into the mouth of a serpent at night;

children.text: tṛptas tat-piśitena satvaram asau tenaiva yātaḥ yathā
children.translated_text: sated quickly on the serpent's flesh, it escaped through that very hole —

children.text: lokāḥ paśyata daivam eva hi nṛṇāṃ vṛddhau kṣaye kāraṇam || BharSt_1.85 ||
children.translated_text: behold, O people! It is fate alone that causes the rise and fall of men. || BharSt_1.85 ||
Laziness is indeed the greatest enemy
dwelling within a person's body;
there is no ally equal to effort —
one who exerts himself never comes to ruin. || BharSt_1.86 ||

children.text: chinno 'pi rohati tar kṣīṇo 'py upacīyate punaś candraḥ |
children.translated_text: Even when cut, a tree grows back; even when waned, the moon waxes full again;

children.text: iti vimṛśantaḥ santaḥ santapyante na duḥkheṣu || BharSt_1.87 ||
children.translated_text: Thus reflecting, the wise are not tormented by sorrows. || BharSt_1.87 ||

children.text: netā yasya bṛhaspatiḥ praharaṇaṃ vajraṃ surāḥ sainikāḥ
children.translated_text: He whose counselor is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, whose weapon is the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>), whose soldiers are the gods,

children.text: svargo durgam anugrahaḥ kila harer airāvato vāraṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: whose fortress is heaven, whose favor comes from <s>Hari</s>, whose elephant is <s>Airāvata</s>—

children.text: ity aiśvarya-balānvito 'pi balabhid bhagnaḥ paraiḥ saṅgare
children.translated_text: even <s>Indra</s> (<s>Balabhid</s>), endowed with such power and sovereignty, was defeated by enemies in battle;

children.text: tad vyaktaṃ nanu daivam eva śaraṇaṃ dhig dhig vṛthā pauruṣam || BharSt_1.88 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, clearly, fate alone is the refuge—alas, alas for the futility of human effort! || BharSt_1.88 ||
The fruit of men's [action] depends on <s>karma</s>;
intelligence follows <s>karma</s>;
nevertheless, one should be of good judgment,
acting only after careful deliberation. || BharSt_1.89 ||

children.text: khalv āto divaseśvarasya kiraṇaiḥ santāḍito mastake
children.translated_text: Indeed, struck on the head by the rays of the lord of day,

children.text: vāñchan deśam anātapaṃ vidhi-vaśāt tālasya mūlaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: seeking a place without heat, by the will of fate he went to the foot of a palm tree;

children.text: tatrāpy asya mahāphalena patatā bhagnaṃ saśabdaṃ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: there too, his head was broken with a loud crash by the falling of a great fruit—

children.text: prāyo gacchati yatra bhāgya-rahitas tatraiva yānty āpadaḥ || BharSt_1.90 ||
children.translated_text: wherever the unfortunate one goes, there indeed misfortunes follow. || BharSt_1.90 ||
The sun and the moon suffer the affliction of eclipses;
the elephant and the serpent also suffer bondage;
seeing even the wise reduced to poverty,

children.text: vidhir aho balavān iti me matiḥ || BharSt_1.91 ||
children.translated_text: my conviction is: 'Ah, fate is indeed powerful!' || BharSt_1.91 ||
Fate creates a jewel among men,
endowed with every virtue, an ornament of the earth;
yet if it destroys that [jewel] in a single moment,

children.text: ced ahaha kaṣṭam apaṇḍitatā vidheḥ || BharSt_1.92 ||
children.translated_text: alas, what folly on the part of Fate! || BharSt_1.92 ||

children.text: patraṃ naiva yadā karīra-viṭape doṣo vasantasya kim
children.translated_text: When there is no leaf on the <s>karīra</s> bush, is it the fault of spring?

children.text: nolūko 'py avaokate yadi divā sūryasya kiṃ dūṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: If the owl cannot see by day, is that a defect of the sun?

children.text: dhārā naiva patanti cātaka-mukhe meghasya kiṃ dūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: If raindrops do not fall into the <s>cātaka</s> bird's mouth, is it the fault of the cloud?

children.text: yat pūrvaṃ vidhinā lalāṭa-likhitaṃ tan mārjituṃ kaḥ kṣamaḥ || BharSt_1.93 ||
children.translated_text: What was formerly inscribed by Fate on the forehead—who is able to erase it? || BharSt_1.93 ||

children.text: namasyāmo devān nanu hatavidhes te 'pi vaśagā
children.translated_text: Shall we worship the gods? But even they are subject to accursed Fate.
Shall Fate be worshipped? But even he gives fruit only according to fixed <s>karma</s>.

children.text: phalaṃ karmāyattaṃ yadi kim amaraiḥ kiṃ ca vidhinā
children.translated_text: If the fruit depends on <s>karma</s>, then what use are the gods, what use is Fate?

children.text: namas tat-karmabhyo vidhir api na yebhyaḥ prabhavati || BharSt_1.94 ||
children.translated_text: Salutation to that <s>karma</s>, over which even Fate has no power! || BharSt_1.94 ||
<s>Brahmā</s>, by whom was confined like a potter within the vessel of the cosmic egg;
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, by whom was cast into the great peril of the ten <s>avatāras</s>;
<s>Rudra</s>, by whom was made to beg for alms with a skull held in his hand;

children.text: sūryo bhrāmyati nityam eva gagane tasmai namaḥ karmaṇe || BharSt_1.95 ||
children.translated_text: the sun revolves forever in the sky—to that <s>Karma</s>, salutation! || BharSt_1.95 ||

children.text: naivākṛtiḥ phalati naivaa kulaṃ na śīlaṃ
children.translated_text: Neither beauty bears fruit, nor family, nor good conduct,

children.text: vidyāpi naiva na ca yatna-kṛtāpi sevā |
children.translated_text: nor learning, nor service rendered with great effort;
it is the fortunes accumulated by former austerities

children.text: kāle phalanti puruṣasya yathaiva vṛkṣāḥ || BharSt_1.96 ||
children.translated_text: that bear fruit for a person in due time, just as trees [bear fruit in season]. || BharSt_1.96 ||
In the forest, in battle, in the midst of enemies, flood, and fire,
in the great ocean, or on the mountain peak,
whether asleep, careless, or standing in a perilous place,
the merits (<s>puṇya</s>) earned in former lives protect [a person]. || BharSt_1.97 ||

children.text: yā sādhūṃś ca khalān karoti viduṣo mūrkhān hitān dveṣiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: She who makes saints into villains, the wise into fools, the well-disposed into haters,

children.text: pratyakṣaṃ kurute parīkṣam amṛtaṃ hālāhalaṃ tat-kṣaṇāt |
children.translated_text: who in an instant makes nectar into <s>hālāhala</s> poison before one's very eyes—

children.text: tām ārādhaya sat-kriyāṃ bhagavatīṃ bhoktuṃ phalaṃ vāñchitaṃ
children.translated_text: propitiate that sovereign lady, Good Action (<s>satkriyā</s>), if you wish to enjoy the desired fruit;

children.text: he sādho vyasanair guṇeṣu vipuleṣv āsthāṃ vṛthā mā kṛthāḥ || BharSt_1.98 ||
children.translated_text: O good man, do not vainly place your trust in abundant virtues [alone], despite calamities. || BharSt_1.98 ||
Whether one performs the mass of actions well or poorly,
the wise person should carefully consider the outcome;
for actions done in excessive haste,
the result is heart-burning, like a thorn-point, until it manifests. || BharSt_1.99 ||

children.text: sthālyāṃ vaidūryamayyāṃ pacati tilakaṇāṃś candanair indhanaughaiḥ
children.translated_text: He cooks sesame seeds in a pot of <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), using heaps of sandalwood as fuel;

children.text: sauvarṇair lāṅgalāgrair vilikhati vasudhām arka-mūlasya hetoḥ |
children.translated_text: he plows the earth with golden ploughshares for the sake of <s>arka</s>-root;

children.text: kṛtvā karpūra-khaṇḍān vṛttim iha kurute kodravāṇāṃ samantāt
children.translated_text: having made camphor into pieces, he makes his livelihood all around from <s>kodrava</s> grain—

children.text: prāpyemāṃ karm-bhūmiṃ na carati manujo yas topa manda-bhāgyaḥ || BharSt_1.100 ||
children.translated_text: the person who, having attained this land of <s>karma</s>, does not perform austerities (<s>tapas</s>), is indeed of wretched fortune. || BharSt_1.100 ||

children.text: majjatv ambhasi yātu meru-śikharaṃ śatruṃ jayatv āhave
children.translated_text: Let him dive into the waters, let him ascend the peak of <s>Meru</s>, let him conquer enemies in battle,

children.text: vāṇijyaṃ kṛṣi-sevane ca sakalā vidyāḥ kalāḥ śikṣatām |
children.translated_text: let him learn all sciences and arts, engage in commerce and agriculture;

children.text: ākāśaṃ vipulaṃ prayātu khagavat kṛtvā prayatnaṃ paraṃ
children.translated_text: let him traverse the vast sky like a bird, making the utmost effort—

children.text: nābhāvyaṃ bhavatīha karma-vaśato bhāvyasya nāśaḥ kutaḥ || BharSt_1.101 ||
children.translated_text: what is not fated cannot come to be; and what is fated—whence its destruction? || BharSt_1.101 ||

children.text: bhīmaṃ vanaṃ bhavati tasya puraṃ pradhānaṃ
children.translated_text: The fearsome forest becomes his chief city;
all people become his kinsmen;
the entire earth becomes full of treasures within reach
for the man who possesses abundant merit (<s>sukṛta</s>) earned in former lives. || BharSt_1.102 ||

children.text: ko lābho guṇisaṅgamaḥ kim asukhaṃ prājñetaraiḥ saṅgatiḥ
children.translated_text: What is gain? The company of the virtuous. What is misery? Association with the unwise.

children.text: kā hāniḥ samaya-cyutir nipuṇatā kā dharma-tattve ratiḥ |
children.translated_text: What is loss? The lapse of propriety. What is skill? Delight in the truth of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: kaḥ śūro vijitendriyaḥ priyatamā kā 'nuvratā kiṃ dhanaṃ
children.translated_text: Who is a hero? He who has conquered the senses. Who is the dearest beloved? A devoted wife. What is wealth?

children.text: vidyā kiṃ sukham apravāsa-gamanaṃ rājyaṃ kim ājñā-phalam || BharSt_1.103 ||
children.translated_text: Learning. What is happiness? Not going abroad. What is sovereignty? The fruit of one's command. || BharSt_1.103 ||
With those poor in harsh speech, rich in kind words, content with their own wives,

children.text: para-parivāda-nivṛttaiḥ kvacit kvacin maṇḍitā vasudhā || BharSt_1.104 ||
children.translated_text: and abstaining from speaking ill of others—by such people is the earth adorned here and there. || BharSt_1.104 ||
Even when one of steadfast nature is humiliated,
the virtue of steadfastness cannot be wiped away;
even when fire is held with its flame facing downward,

children.text: nādhaḥ śikhā yāti kadācid eva || BharSt_1.105 ||
children.translated_text: the flame never goes downward. || BharSt_1.105 ||
He whose heart is not pierced by the arrows of a beloved's sidelong glances,
whose mind is not burned by the fire of poverty's anguish,
who is not dragged by the noose of greed toward abundant sense-objects—

children.text: loka-trayaṃ jayati kṛtsnam idaṃ sa dhīraḥ || BharSt_1.106 ||
children.translated_text: that steadfast one conquers all three worlds entirely. || BharSt_1.106 ||
By even one hero,
the surface of the earth is trodden under foot—
[so too] by the sun alone,
with its widely blazing radiance. || BharSt_1.107 ||

children.text: vahnis tasya jalāyate jala-nidhiḥ kulyāyate tat-kṣaṇān
children.translated_text: Fire becomes water for him; the ocean becomes a mere stream in an instant;
<s>Meru</s> becomes a small pebble; the lion instantly becomes a deer;
the serpent becomes a garland; poison becomes a shower of nectar
for him in whose person blossoms the most beloved virtue of the entire world. || BharSt_1.108 ||
Modesty, the mother of a flood of virtues, like one's own mother—
following [her], who is of utterly pure heart,
the heroic gladly give up even their lives,
those devoted to the practice of truth, but never their pledged word. || BharSt_1.109 ||
The Century on Love (<s>Śṛṅgāraśataka</s>) of <s>Bhartṛhari</s>.
<s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Svayambhu</s>, and <s>Hari</s>—[even they] were made forever
into household servants by the doe-eyed ones;
to that blessed one whose deeds defy the reach of words, of wondrous character,
to that <s>Bhagavān</s> who bears the crocodile-banner (<s>Makaradhvaja</s>, i.e. <s>Kāmadeva</s>)—salutation! || BharSt_2.1 ||
With a smile, with feeling, with modesty, with fear,
with averted half-sidelong glances,
with words, with quarrels of jealousy, with playfulness—
indeed, with all their expressions, women are a bond. || BharSt_2.2 ||
Sidelong glances curved with the artfulness of brows,
tender words and laughter ending in bashfulness,
movements and pauses languid with playfulness—

children.text: strīṇām etad bhūṣaṇaṃ cāyudhaṃ ca || BharSt_2.3 ||
children.translated_text: these are both the ornaments and the weapons of women. || BharSt_2.3 ||

children.text: kvacit sa-bhrū-bhaṅgaiḥ kvacid api ca lajjā-parigataiḥ
children.translated_text: Sometimes with frowning brows, sometimes with bashful reserve,

children.text: kvacid bhūri-trastaiḥ kvacid api ca līlā-vilalitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: sometimes greatly alarmed, sometimes with playful coquetry—
with these turnings of the eyes, graced by <s>Madana</s> (Love),
the directions seem scattered with clusters of trembling blue lotuses [by] maidens. || BharSt_2.4 ||
A face blooming like the moon, eyes rivaling the lotus,

children.text: varṇaḥ svarṇam apākariṣṇur alinī-jiṣṇuḥ kacānāṃ cayaḥ |
children.translated_text: a complexion that puts gold to shame, tresses of hair that defeat the line of bees,
breasts that rob the frontal globes of elephants of their pride, a weighty expanse of hips,

children.text: vācāṃ hāri ca mārdavaṃ yuvatīṣu svābhāvikaṃ maṇḍanam || BharSt_2.5 ||
children.translated_text: and the captivating softness of speech—in young women, these are nature's own adornment. || BharSt_2.5 ||
A smile slightly naive, the wealth of a glance with restlessly darting pupils,
the play of words rich with expressions of fresh coquetry,
the beginning of movements accompanied by the graceful apparatus of tender sprout-like gestures—

children.text: spṛśantyās tāruṇyaṃ kim iva na hi ramyaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ || BharSt_2.6 ||
children.translated_text: of the doe-eyed woman entering youth, what indeed is not charming? || BharSt_2.6 ||

children.text: draṣṭavyeṣu kim uttamaṃ mṛgadṛśaḥ prema-prasannaṃ mukhaṃ
children.translated_text: What is best among sights? The doe-eyed one's face, radiant with love.

children.text: ghrātaveṣv api kiṃ tad-āsya-pavanaḥ śravyeṣu kiṃ tad-vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: What is best among scents? The breath from her mouth. What is best to hear? Her words.

children.text: kiṃ svādyeṣu tad-oṣṭha-pallava-rasaḥ spṛśyeṣu kiṃ tad-vapurdhyeyaṃ
children.translated_text: What is best to taste? The nectar of her tender lip. What is best to touch? Her body. What is best to contemplate?

children.text: kiṃ nava-yauvane sahṛdayaiḥ sarvatra tad-vibhramāḥ || BharSt_2.7 ||
children.translated_text: For the sensitive heart, her coquettish ways [are best] everywhere—in her fresh youth. || BharSt_2.7 ||
These young women, with the jingling of moving clusters of bracelets and girdle-bells,
whose anklet-sounds put royal swans to shame—

children.text: kurvanti kasya na mano vivaśaṃ taruṇyo
children.translated_text: whose mind do they not overpower,
with sidelong glances resembling those of startled, innocent deer? || BharSt_2.8 ||
Her body marked with saffron paste,
her necklace trembling upon her fair breasts,
her feet [adorned with] anklets ringing like swans—

children.text: kaṃ na vaśīkurute bhuvi rāmā || BharSt_2.9 ||
children.translated_text: what woman (<s>rāmā</s>) on earth does not bring [men] under her sway? || BharSt_2.9 ||
Surely those best of poets spoke contrarily,

children.text: ye nityam āhur abalā iti kāminīs tāḥ |
children.translated_text: who always called those beloveds 'the weak' (<s>abalā</s>);
by whom, with the falling of glances with restlessly darting pupils,

children.text: śakrādayo 'pi vijitās tv abalāḥ kathaṃ tāḥ || BharSt_2.10 ||
children.translated_text: even <s>Indra</s> (<s>Śakra</s>) and the rest were conquered—how then are they 'weak'? || BharSt_2.10 ||
Surely the crocodile-bannered one (<s>Makaradhvaja</s>, i.e. <s>Kāmadeva</s>) obeys her command, the fair-browed one,
since he acts upon whatever is indicated by the movement of her eyes. || BharSt_2.11 ||

children.text: keśāḥ saṃyaminaḥ śruter api paraṃ pāraṃ gate locane
children.translated_text: Her hair is ascetic (<s>saṃyamin</s>); her eyes have gone beyond even the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>śruti</s>);

children.text: antar-vaktram api svabhāva-śuci-bhīḥ kīrṇaṃ dvijānāṃ gaṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: even the interior of her mouth, naturally pure and holy, is crowded with hosts of the twice-born (<s>dvija</s>, i.e. teeth);
her breast-vessels are beautiful from the constant residence of the liberated (<s>mukta</s>, i.e. pearls)—

children.text: tanvi vapuḥ praśāntam api terāgaṃ karoty eva naḥ || BharSt_2.12 ||
children.translated_text: thus, O slender one, your body, though tranquil, causes desire (<s>rāga</s>) in us. || BharSt_2.12 ||

children.text: mugdhe dhānuṣkatā keyam apūrvā tvayi dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: O innocent one, what unprecedented archery-skill is seen in you,

children.text: yayā vidhyasi cetāṃsi guṇair eva na sāyakaiḥ || BharSt_2.13 ||
children.translated_text: by which you pierce hearts with virtues alone, not with arrows! || BharSt_2.13 ||

children.text: sati pradīpe saty agnau satsu tārāravīnduṣu |
children.translated_text: Though there be lamps, though there be fire, though there be stars, sun, and moon,

children.text: vinā me mṛga-śāvākṣyā tamo-bhūtam idaṃ jagat || BharSt_2.14 ||
children.translated_text: without my deer-fawn-eyed beloved, this world is nothing but darkness. || BharSt_2.14 ||

children.text: udvṛttaḥ stana-bhāra eṣa tarale netre cale bhrū-late
children.translated_text: Let this swelling burden of breasts, these restless eyes, these moving vine-like brows,

children.text: rāgādhiṣṭhitam oṣṭha-pallavam idaṃ kurvantu nāma vyathām |
children.translated_text: these lip-petals overlaid with passion—let them cause distress;
[but] like a rosary of auspicious letters inscribed by the Flower-armed (<s>Puṣpāyudha</s>, i.e. <s>Kāma</s>) himself,

children.text: madhyasthāpi karoti tāpam adhikaṃ romāvaliḥ kena sā || BharSt_2.15 ||
children.translated_text: why does that line of hair on the belly (<s>romāvalī</s>), though standing neutral, cause even greater torment? || BharSt_2.15 ||
With a face like the moonstone, with great sapphires for hair,

children.text: karābhyāṃ padmarāgābhyāṃ reje ratnamayīva sā || BharSt_2.16 ||
children.translated_text: with hands like rubies (<s>padmarāga</s>)—she shone as if made of jewels. || BharSt_2.16 ||
With the heavy burden of her breasts, with her face shining like the moon,

children.text: śanaiś-carābhyāṃ pādābhyāṃ reje grahamayīva sā || BharSt_2.17 ||
children.translated_text: with feet moving slowly like <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn)—she shone as if made of planets. || BharSt_2.17 ||

children.text: tasyāḥ stanau yadi ghanau jaghanaṃ ca hāri
children.translated_text: If her breasts are firm, her hips charming,

children.text: vaktraṃ ca cāru tava citta kim ākulatvam |
children.translated_text: and her face beautiful—O heart, why this agitation?

children.text: puṇyaṃ kuruṣva yadi teṣu tavāsti vāñchā
children.translated_text: Perform merit (<s>puṇya</s>) if you have desire for these;

children.text: puṇyair vinā na hi bhavanti samīhitārthāḥ || BharSt_2.18 ||
children.translated_text: for without merit, desired objects do not come to be. || BharSt_2.18 ||
These, fragrant with the fresh splendor of youth, powerful in the prowess of mature passion,
guarantors of victory for <s>Smara</s> (the god of Love),
thieves of the mind, O heart, uniquely weighty with novel transformations,

children.text: vilāsa-vyāpārāḥ kim api vijayante mṛga-dṛśām || BharSt_2.19 ||
children.translated_text: the amorous acts of the doe-eyed ones conquer in some ineffable way. || BharSt_2.19 ||
Sweet with affection, overflowing with love, having attained the state of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment),
sweet in utterance, mostly innocent, revealing delight,
naturally charming, moist with trust, bestowing the arising of <s>Smara</s> (desire)—

children.text: rahasi kim api svairālāpā haranti mṛgīdṛśām || BharSt_2.20 ||
children.translated_text: in solitude, the spontaneous murmurings of the doe-eyed ones steal [the heart] in some ineffable way. || BharSt_2.20 ||
Resting again and again in the shade
of forest trees, a certain slender woman wandered;
with the upper garment from her breasts, lifted by her hand,
she was warding off the rays of the moon. || BharSt_2.21 ||
In her absence, we desire merely to see her;
having seen her, we long only for the joy of embrace;
when the long-eyed one is embraced, then again we wish
for the non-difference of our two bodies. || BharSt_2.22 ||
<s>Mālatī</s> [jasmine] on the head, a yawn on the face,
sandal paste mixed with saffron upon the body,
the beloved, languid with passion, upon the chest —
this is heaven; the rest is mere scripture. || BharSt_2.23 ||

children.text: prāṅ mām eti manāg anāgata-rasaṃ jātābhilāṣāṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: First she approaches me, slightly lacking the taste of what is yet to come, then with desire awakened,

children.text: savrīḍaṃ tad anu ślathodyamam atha pradhvasta-dhairyaṃ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: then bashfully, then with slackening effort, and then again with boldness dissolved,
then tender with love, in enviable and intense secret play, growing bold,
delightful with the heightened pleasure of drawing limbs together without restraint — such is the love of a woman of noble family. || BharSt_2.24 ||
Of those who have fallen upon the chest, their braided hair loosened,
their eyes half-closed, slightly opened,
their cheeks moist with the sweat of amorous exertion — the lip-
nectar of such brides the fortunate ones drink. || BharSt_2.25 ||
Of those whose eyes are half-closed,
the essence of love's pleasure shines forth in mutual understanding;
mutually confirmed between lovers,
this alone is the true extinguishing of desire. || BharSt_2.26 ||
This is improper and out of order for men,

children.text: yad iha jarāsv api manmathā vikārāḥ |
children.translated_text: that even in old age the agitations of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) persist;

children.text: tad api ca na kṛtaṃ nitambinīnāṃ
children.translated_text: and yet nature has not granted to broad-hipped women
a life or passion that lasts only until the breasts sag. || BharSt_2.27 ||

children.text: rājas-tṛṣṇāmburāśer na hi jagati gataḥ kaścid evāvasānaṃ
children.translated_text: Truly no one in this world has ever reached the end of the ocean of passionate thirst;

children.text: ko vārtho 'rthaiḥ prabhūtaiḥ sva-vapuṣi galite yauvane sānurāge |
children.translated_text: and what use are abundant riches when youth with its ardour has departed from one's body?
Let us go to the dwelling while the beauty of our beloveds, whose eyes resemble blossoming blue lotuses, is not yet

children.text: rūpaṃ jhaṭiti na jarayā lupyate preyasīnām || BharSt_2.28 ||
children.translated_text: suddenly stolen away by old age, overrunning them again and again. || BharSt_2.28 ||
The sole abode of passion, the cause of attaining the great suffering of a hundred hells, the seed of
delusion's birth, a bank of clouds obscuring the moon of knowledge,
the one friend of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), displaying a series of manifold and evident faults —

children.text: loke 'smin na hy artha-vraja-kula-bhavana-yauvanād anyad asti || BharSt_2.29 ||
children.translated_text: there is nothing else in this world besides the household of youth with its throngs of wealth. || BharSt_2.29 ||
A rain-cloud for the tree of love, a rushing stream of playful delight,
a dear kinsman of <s>Pradyumna</s> (the god of love), an ocean of pearl-like clever speech,
the purifying moon for the <s>cakora</s> birds that are slender women's eyes, a treasure of beauty and fortune —

children.text: dhanyaḥ ko 'pi na vikriyāṃ kalayati prāpte nave yauvane || BharSt_2.30 ||
children.translated_text: what blessed one is there who remains unaffected when fresh youth arrives? || BharSt_2.30 ||

In this worthless <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), how could those of pure intellect compose their minds, when their steadiness is shattered by the stain of servitude at the doors of wicked kings'
palaces and the entanglements of worldly attachment?

children.text: yady etāḥ prodyad-indu-dyuti-nicaya-bhṛto na syur ambhoja-netrāḥ
children.translated_text: If only these lotus-eyed young women did not exist, bearing the splendour of the rising moon's radiance,
with tinkling girdle-chains and waists bending under the weight of their breasts! || BharSt_2.31 ||
When on <s>Himavat</s> (the Himalaya), in caves frequented by <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings), beneath trees bent by the shoulder of <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) bull,
on rock-surfaces washed by the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in that auspicious abode,

children.text: kaḥ kurvīta śiraḥ praṇāma-malinaṃ mlānaṃ manasvī jano
children.translated_text: what spirited person would bow his head in degrading obeisance,

children.text: yad-vitrasta-kuraṅga-śāva-nayanā na syuḥ smarāstraṃ striyaḥ || BharSt_2.32 ||
children.translated_text: if women, whose eyes are like those of a startled fawn, were not the weapons of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love)? || BharSt_2.32 ||
O <s>Saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), the path to your end is not far away;

children.text: antarā dustarā na syur yadi te madirekṣaṇām || BharSt_2.33 ||
children.translated_text: if only the intoxicating-eyed ones were not impassable obstacles in between. || BharSt_2.33 ||
Give to the forest deer mouthfuls of <s>kuśa</s> grass
whose roots have been cut against stone edges, of bamboo-green hue;
or give to the brides betel leaves pale as the cheeks
of <s>Śaka</s> maidens, torn with reddened fingertips. || BharSt_2.34 ||
All those pleasures of the senses are empty, tasteless through renunciation, sinful in their objects —

children.text: jugupsyantāṃ yad vā nanu sakala-doṣāspadam iti |
children.translated_text: let them be despised, for they are indeed the seat of every fault;

children.text: tathāpy etad-bhūmau nahi para-hitāt puṇyam adhikaṃ
children.translated_text: nevertheless, on this earth there is no merit greater than benefiting others,

children.text: na cāsmin saṃsāre kuvalaya-dṛśo ramyam aparam || BharSt_2.35 ||
children.translated_text: nor in this <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is there anything more lovely than lotus-eyed women. || BharSt_2.35 ||
The true fruit of love in this world is the oneness of mind between two;

children.text: anya-citta-kṛte kāme śavayor iva saṅgamaḥ || BharSt_2.35*1 ||
children.translated_text: love directed at one whose heart is elsewhere is like the coupling of corpses. || BharSt_2.35*1 ||
Setting aside jealousy and considering the matter,
let noble persons speak with propriety:
should one serve the slopes of mountains
or those of smiling, amorous women? || BharSt_2.36 ||

children.text: saṃsāre svapna-sāre pariṇati-tarale dve gatī paṇḍitānāṃ
children.translated_text: In this <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), as insubstantial as a dream and changeable in its outcomes, the wise have two paths:
for those whose minds are refined by the raft of the nectar-waters of knowledge of truth, let time pass somehow or other;
but if not, then in the company of charming women with full, dense, heavy breasts and buttocks,
with hands playfully concealed upon their broad pelvic regions. || BharSt_2.37 ||
Let one make one's abode in the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, which destroy sin,

children.text: stana-dvaye taruṇyā vā manohāriṇi hāriṇi || BharSt_2.38 ||
children.translated_text: or upon the pair of breasts of a young woman, which captivate the mind. || BharSt_2.38 ||

children.text: kim iha bahubhir uktair yukti-śūnyaiḥ pralāpairdvayam
children.translated_text: Why say much here with pointless prattle devoid of reason? Two things
should always be pursued by men in this world:
the youth of beautiful women, swaying with the play of fresh intoxication,

children.text: stana-bhara-parikhinnaṃ yauvanaṃ vā vanaṃ vā || BharSt_2.39 ||
children.translated_text: with waists bowed under the weight of their breasts — or the forest. || BharSt_2.39 ||
Truly, O people, I speak without partiality;
in all the seven worlds this is the truth:
there is nothing more enchanting than broad-hipped women,

children.text: duḥkhaika-hetur na ca kaścid anyaḥ || BharSt_2.40 ||
children.translated_text: nor is there any other sole cause of suffering. || BharSt_2.40 ||
'Beloved!' 'Blue-lotus-eyed!' 'With broad, heavy hips!' 'With swelling,
high, uplifted breasts!' 'Lotus-faced!' 'Fair-browed!' —

children.text: dṛṣṭvā mādyati modate 'bhiramate prastauti vidvān api
children.translated_text: seeing her thus, even the learned man grows intoxicated, delights, is enraptured, and sings praises

children.text: pratyakṣāśuci-bhastrikāṃ striyam aho mohasya duśceṣṭitam || BharSt_2.41 ||
children.translated_text: of a woman, who is manifestly an impure bellows of skin — ah, the wicked work of delusion! || BharSt_2.41 ||
When remembered, she causes torment; when seen, she causes madness;

children.text: spṛṣṭā bhavati mohāya sā nāma dayitā katham || BharSt_2.42 ||
children.translated_text: when touched, she causes delusion — how then can she be called 'beloved'? || BharSt_2.42 ||
She is nectar only so long as she remains within the range of sight;

children.text: cakṣuṣ-pathād atītā tu viṣād apy atiricyate || BharSt_2.43 ||
children.translated_text: but once she has passed beyond the path of the eyes, she surpasses even poison. || BharSt_2.43 ||

children.text: nāmṛtaṃ na viṣaṃ kiñcid etāṃ muktvā nitambinīm |
children.translated_text: There is nothing that is neither nectar nor poison except this broad-hipped woman;
she herself, when in love, is a creeper of nectar; when estranged, a vine of poison. || BharSt_2.44 ||
A whirlpool of doubts, a realm of impropriety, a citadel of reckless deeds,
a storehouse of faults, a field of distrust made of a hundred deceptions,
an obstacle to heaven's gate, a gateway to the city of hell, a casket of every illusion —

children.text: strī-yantraṃ kena sṛṣṭaṃ viṣam amṛtamayaṃ prāṇi-lokasya pāśaḥ || BharSt_2.45 ||
children.translated_text: by whom was this machine called 'woman' created? Poison made of nectar, a snare for all living beings! || BharSt_2.45 ||

children.text: no satyena mṛgāṅka eṣa vadanī-bhūto na cendīvaradvandvaṃ
children.translated_text: In truth the moon has not become her face, nor has a pair of blue lotuses

children.text: locanatāṃ gata na kanakair apy aṅga-yaṣṭiḥ kṛtā |
children.translated_text: become her eyes, nor is her body-staff made of gold;

children.text: kintv evaṃ kavibhiḥ pratārita-manās tattvaṃ vijānann api
children.translated_text: yet, with the mind thus deceived by poets, even while knowing the truth,

children.text: tvaṅ-māṃsāsthi-mayaṃ vapur mṛga-dṛśāṃ mando janaḥ sevate || BharSt_2.46 ||
children.translated_text: the foolish person serves the body of doe-eyed women, which is but skin, flesh, and bone. || BharSt_2.46 ||
The natural graces of playful women —
those very graces flash in the heart of the deluded one;
the redness of the lotus is established by nature,
yet the bee buzzes around it in vain. || BharSt_2.47 ||
They bewitch, they intoxicate, they mock,
they rebuke, they delight, they cause despair;
entering the tender hearts of men,

children.text: kiṃ nāma vāma-nayanā na samācaranti || BharSt_2.47*1 ||
children.translated_text: what do these side-glancing women not do? || BharSt_2.47*1 ||
That lotus-face of the slender woman, which steals the radiance of the full moon, of surpassing beauty,
where lip-nectar resides —

children.text: idaṃ tat kiṃ pāka-druma-phalam idānīm atirasavyatīte 'smin
children.translated_text: is this the fruit of a ripening tree, excessively sweet now,

children.text: kāle viṣam iva bhaviṣyty asukhadam || BharSt_2.48 ||
children.translated_text: which in the course of time will become as unpleasant as poison? || BharSt_2.48 ||
With the abode of unfolding waves of three folds (at the waist), with a pair of prominent full breasts from which arise
a pair of <s>cakravāka</s> birds, shining with a lotus-face,
this river bearing the form of a woman does not care at all — beware!

children.text: saṃsārārṇava-majjanaṃ yadi tadā dūreṇa santyajyatām || BharSt_2.49 ||
children.translated_text: If one does not wish to drown in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), then let it be abandoned from afar. || BharSt_2.49 ||

children.text: jalpanti sārdham anyena paśyanty anyaṃ savibhramāḥ |
children.translated_text: They talk with one man, they cast tremulous glances at another,

children.text: hṛd-gataṃ cintayanty anyaṃ priyaḥ ko nāma yoṣitām || BharSt_2.50 ||
children.translated_text: and in their hearts they think of yet another — who then is truly dear to women? || BharSt_2.50 ||

children.text: madhu tiṣṭhati vāci yoṣitāṃ hṛdi hālāhalam eva kevalam |
children.translated_text: Honey dwells on the lips of women, but in their hearts there is nothing but <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison);

children.text: ataeva nipīyate 'dharo hṛdayaṃ muṣṭibhir eva tāḍyate || BharSt_2.51 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the lip is sipped, while the heart is struck with fists. || BharSt_2.51 ||
Retreat, O friend, far from this fire of poisonous side-glances,
from this woman-serpent, treacherous by nature, bearing the hood of coquetry;
one bitten by an ordinary serpent can be healed with medicines,
but one seized by this clever female serpent — not even sorcerers can cure. || BharSt_2.52 ||
Cast into this ocean of worldly existence by the fisherman <s>Makara-ketana</s> (Love, whose banner bears the sea-monster)
is the hook called 'woman';
with it, mortal fish greedy for the bait of her lip-
flesh are swiftly dragged out and roasted in the fire of passion. || BharSt_2.53 ||
In the wilderness of a woman's body, impassable with the mountains of her breasts,

children.text: mā saṃcara manaḥ pāntha tatrāste smara-taskaraḥ || BharSt_2.54 ||
children.translated_text: do not wander, O mind-traveller, for there lurks <s>Smara</s> (Love), the robber. || BharSt_2.54 ||
By that long, darting, radiant, serpent-like (glance), with the lustre of a blue lotus —

children.text: nīlābja-dyutināhinā param ahaṃ dṛṣṭo na tac-cakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: by that serpent of her eyes — I have been bitten, not by an ordinary snake;

children.text: dṛṣṭe santi cikitsakā diśi diśi prāyeṇa darmārthino
children.translated_text: for snakebite there are healers to be found in every direction, mostly seeking payment,

children.text: mugdhākṣkṣaṇa-vīkṣitasya na hi me vaidyo na cāpy auṣadham || BharSt_2.55 ||
children.translated_text: but for one bitten by the glance of a doe-eyed woman, there is for me no physician and no medicine. || BharSt_2.55 ||
'Here is sweet song, here is dance, here is aesthetic delight,
here wafts fragrance, here is the touch of breasts' —
thus, led astray by the senses whose ultimate aim is lost,
I have been deceived by these five rogues who pretend to serve my interest. || BharSt_2.56 ||

children.text: na gamyo mantrāṇāṃ na ca bhavati bhaiṣajya-viṣayo
children.translated_text: It is not accessible to <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulas), nor does it fall within the scope of medicine,

children.text: na cāpi pradhvaṃsaṃ vrajati vividhaiḥ śāntika-śataiḥ |
children.translated_text: nor does it perish through hundreds of various pacification rites;

children.text: bhramāveśād aṅge kam api vidadhad bhaṅgam asakṛt
children.translated_text: inflicting upon the body some indescribable contortion through the onset of madness, again and again,

children.text: smarāpasmāro 'yaṃ bhramayati dṛśaṃ ghūrṇayati ca || BharSt_2.57 ||
children.translated_text: this epilepsy of <s>Smara</s> (Love) makes the eyes wander and the head spin. || BharSt_2.57 ||

children.text: jāty-andhāya ca durmukhāya ca jarājīrṇā khilāṅgāya ca
children.translated_text: To one blind from birth, to one ugly of face, to one wasted and decrepit with age and broken-limbed,

children.text: grāmīṇāya ca duṣkulāya ca galat-kuṣṭhābhibhūtāya ca |
children.translated_text: to a rustic, to one of low birth, to one overwhelmed by spreading leprosy —
when courtesans give their enchanting bodily beauty, trusting in a mere fraction of their charms,
who would take pleasure in such women, who are like creepers of discrimination in name only? || BharSt_2.58 ||
That courtesan is the flame of <s>Madana</s> (Love),
fed with the fuel of beauty;
in which are offered as oblations by lovers
their youth and their wealth. || BharSt_2.59 ||

children.text: kaś cumbati kula-puruṣo veśyādhara-pallavaṃ manojñam api |
children.translated_text: What man of noble family would kiss the charming lip-petal of a courtesan,
which is but a spittoon for soldiers, thieves, servants, actors, and rascals? || BharSt_2.60 ||
Blessed indeed are those whose minds remain unchanged
upon seeing the form of women with wide, bright eyes,
with breasts heavy and swollen with the pride of youth,

children.text: dṛṣṭvākṛtiṃ vikṛtim eti mano na yeṣām || BharSt_2.61 ||
children.translated_text: and with creepers of three folds gleaming above their slender waists. || BharSt_2.61 ||
O girl, these slow, playfully half-closed glances —

children.text: kiṃ kṣipyante virama-virama vyartha eṣa śramas te |
children.translated_text: why do you cast them? Cease, cease — this effort of yours is in vain;

children.text: sampraty anye vayam uparataṃ bālyam āsthā vanānte
children.translated_text: we are now different persons, our childhood is past, our abode is in the forest's end,

children.text: kṣīṇo mohas tṛṇam iva jagaj-jālam ālokayāmaḥ || BharSt_2.62 ||
children.translated_text: our delusion is spent — we behold the snare of the world as but a blade of grass. || BharSt_2.62 ||

children.text: iyaṃ bālā māṃ praty anavaratam indīvara-dalaprabhā
children.translated_text: This girl ceaselessly casts at me a long glance

children.text: cīraṃ cakṣuḥ kṣipati kim abhipretam anayā |
children.translated_text: with the radiance of a blue lotus petal — what is her intention?
My delusion is gone, the feverish flame of the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (Love), that savage,

children.text: jvālā śāntā tad api na varākī viramati || BharSt_2.63 ||
children.translated_text: is extinguished — yet the poor girl does not desist. || BharSt_2.63 ||

children.text: kiṃ kandarpa karaṃ kadarthayasi re kodaṇḍa-ṭaṅkāritaṃ
children.translated_text: O <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), why do you torment your hand by stringing the bow?

children.text: re re kokila komalaṃ kala-ravaṃ kiṃ vā vṛthā jalpasi |
children.translated_text: And O cuckoo, why do you warble your soft, melodious notes in vain?
O charming girl, enough of those tender, artful, sweet, and rolling sidelong glances —
my mind abides in the nectar of meditation upon the feet of <s>Candra-cūḍa</s> (Śiva, the moon-crested one). || BharSt_2.64 ||
Even in separation, there is union indeed
for those whose minds are mutually joined;
but if the heart itself is torn asunder,
the one in company feels separation all the more keenly. || BharSt_2.65 ||

children.text: kiṃ gatena yadi sā na jīvati
children.translated_text: "What use is going home if she is no longer alive?
And even if my beloved still breathes, what then?"
Thus musing, gazing at the garland of fresh rain-clouds,
the traveler does not proceed to his home. (BharSt_2.66)
Desist, O wise ones, from the company of women — that pleasure which is fleeting as a moment!
Cultivate instead the companionship of the women named Compassion, Friendship, and Wisdom.
For surely in hell, the full, rounded breasts adorned with pearl necklaces
will not be your refuge, nor will the buttocks girded with jingling jeweled belts. (BharSt_2.67)
When, through devoted practice of <s>Yoga</s>, the mind and self have grown thin,

children.text: maitrī sphurati kṛtinas tasya kim u taiḥ |
children.translated_text: and unbroken friendship shines forth between them — for that fortunate one, what use are these:
the sweet talk of loved ones, the honey of their lips, the moon-like beauty of their faces,
the fragrance of their sighs, and the pleasures of embracing their pitcher-like, budding breasts? (BharSt_2.68)
When there was ignorance, born of the advance of the darkness of desire (<s>Smara</s>),

children.text: tadā dṛṣṭa-nārī-mayam idam aśeṣaṃ jagad iti |
children.translated_text: then this entire world appeared to consist of nothing but women.
Now, for us whose vision has been anointed with the sharper collyrium of discrimination,

children.text: samībhūtā dṛṣṭis tribhuvanam api brahma manute || BharSt_2.69 ||
children.translated_text: our sight has become unified — even the three worlds appear as <s>Brahman</s>. (BharSt_2.69)
Only so long does the lamp of pure discernment
shine even for the wise,
as they are not struck by the glances
from the restless corners of the eyes of doe-eyed women. (BharSt_2.70)
Talk of renouncing worldly attachments exists only in the words
of those scholars whose mouths are loud with the scriptures alone;
yet the hips adorned with girdle-strings knotted with red gems —
of women with lotus eyes — who is able to forsake them? (BharSt_2.71)
He who is a deceiver of himself and others,
that false scholar who condemns young women —
for even the fruit of <s>tapas</s> (austerity)
is heaven, and in heaven too there are <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs). (BharSt_2.72)
There are heroes on earth capable of splitting the frontal globes of maddened elephants,
and some are skilled even in slaying fierce lions;
but I declare: among the mighty, those who can forcefully
crush the pride of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) are rare indeed among men. (BharSt_2.73)

children.text: san-mārge tāvad āste prabhavati ca naras tāvad evendriyāṇāṃ
