children.translated_text: A man stays on the righteous path only so long, he masters his senses only so long,

children.text: lajjāṃ tāvad vidhatte vinayam api samālambate tāvad eva |
children.translated_text: he maintains modesty only so long, and upholds decorum only so long,
as these glance-arrows — released from the bow of the eyebrows, entering the pathway of the ears, dark-feathered —

children.text: yāval līlāvatīnāṃ hṛdi na dhṛtimuṣo dṛṣṭi-bāṇāḥ patanti || BharSt_2.74 ||
children.translated_text: of playful women do not fall upon his heart and steal his resolve. (BharSt_2.74)
When, in the frenzy of wild passion,
women set about their endeavors,
even <s>Brahmā</s> himself is truly
helpless to place an obstacle there. (BharSt_2.75)
Greatness, learning,
noble birth, and discrimination last only so long
as the fire of the five-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>)
does not blaze in one's limbs. (BharSt_2.76)
Even one learned in the scriptures, of excellent lineage, and deeply afflicted —
rare indeed in this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) is one who becomes a vessel for the good path;
for in this world, the crooked creeper of the eyebrow of sidelong-glancing women

children.text: vāmākṣīṇāṃ bhavati kuṭilā bhrū-latā kuñcikeva || BharSt_2.77 ||
children.translated_text: serves as a key that opens the gate of the city of hell. (BharSt_2.77)
Emaciated, one-eyed, lame, without ears, with a maimed tail,
covered in sores, dripping with pus, his body enveloped by hundreds of swarms of worms,
starving, wasted, aged, his neck stuck in the shard of a pot —

children.text: śunīm anveti śvā hatam api ca hanty eva madanaḥ || BharSt_2.78 ||
children.translated_text: even such a dog follows after a bitch; truly <s>Madana</s> (Love) slays even the slain. (BharSt_2.78)
The seal of womanhood, victorious emblem of the Flower-armed one (<s>Kāma</s>), bestower of all wealth and prosperity —

children.text: ye mūḍhāḥ pravihāya yānti kudhiyo mithyā-phalānveṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: those fools of poor understanding who abandon it and pursue illusory rewards,

children.text: te tenaiva nihatya nirdayataraṃ nagnīkṛtā muṇḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: are ruthlessly struck down by that very god, stripped naked, heads shaved —

children.text: kecit pañca-śikhī-kṛtāś ca jaṭilāḥ kāpālikāś cāpare || BharSt_2.79 ||
children.translated_text: some made into five-tufted ascetics, some into matted-haired ones, and others into <s>Kāpālikas</s>. (BharSt_2.79)
Even <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, and other such sages who lived on wind, water, and leaves,
upon merely beholding the lovely lotus-face of a woman, fell into delusion.

children.text: śālyannaṃ sa-ghṛtaṃ payo-dadhi-yutaṃ ye bhuñjate mānavāsteṣām
children.translated_text: As for those men who feast on rice with ghee, milk, and curds —

children.text: indriya-nigraho yadi bhaved vindhyaḥ plavet sāgare || BharSt_2.80 ||
children.translated_text: if they could restrain their senses, then the <s>Vindhya</s> mountains would float upon the ocean! (BharSt_2.80)
Breezes bearing fragrance, treetops with fresh tender shoots,
the beloved <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) birds sweetly singing, yearning for the lovely moon,
the moon-like faces of young brides with sparse, languid drops of perspiration —

children.text: prasarati madhau dhātryāṃ jāto na kasya guṇodayaḥ || BharSt_2.81 ||
children.translated_text: when spring spreads forth on earth, in whom does an upsurge of passion not arise? (BharSt_2.81)
This sweet season, made sweeter by the melodious
calls of the <s>kokila</s> (cuckoo) and the breezes of the <s>Malaya</s> mountain,
destroys the embodied beings who are separated from their beloved;
alas, in adversity, even nectar turns to poison! (BharSt_2.82)
A dwelling with the beloved nearby, languid with amorous play, whispering sweet nothings,
the melodious call of the female <s>kokila</s> in the ear, a smiling bower of creepers,

children.text: goṣṭhī sat-kavibhiḥ samaṃ katipayair mugdhāḥ sudhāṃśoḥ karāḥ
children.translated_text: conversation with a few good poets, the gentle rays of the moon —

children.text: keṣāṃcit sukhayanti cātra hṛdayaṃ caitre vicitrāḥ kṣapāḥ || BharSt_2.83 ||
children.translated_text: these enchanting nights of <s>Caitra</s> (spring month) gladden the hearts of some fortunate ones. (BharSt_2.83)
O traveler! The blossoming clusters on the mango trees, which fan the flame of separation from women,
are now gazed upon with longing by the female <s>kokila</s> birds.
And these breezes from the <s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s> (sandalwood) mountains, moving forward laden with the fragrance of fresh <s>pāṭalā</s> flowers,
spread a canopy of languor and fatigue. (BharSt_2.84)
Let the pride of loving women
hold its place in their hearts
only so long as the breeze from the <s>Malaya</s> mountain
does not blow, fragrant with sandalwood trees. (BharSt_2.85)
When the horizon is saturated with the intoxicating fragrance
borne by masses of mango-blossom filaments,
and the bees are sweetly, sweetly agitated,
who would not feel longing in the spring? (BharSt_2.86)
Doe-eyed women moist with perfectly clear sandalwood paste,
fountain-chambers, flowers, and moonlight,
a gentle breeze, jasmine blossoms, a pure rooftop terrace —

children.text: grīṣme madaṃ ca madanaṃ ca vivardhayanti || BharSt_2.87 ||
children.translated_text: in summer, these increase both intoxication and desire. (BharSt_2.87)
Garlands with heart-pleasing fragrance, the breeze of fans, moonbeams,
pollen, lotus ponds, sandalwood dust, clear wine,
a clean upper-story terrace, thin garments, lotus-eyed women —

children.text: nidāgha-rtāv etad vilasati labhante sukṛtinaḥ || BharSt_2.88 ||
children.translated_text: in the summer season, these delights shine forth and are enjoyed by the fortunate. (BharSt_2.88)
The moon shining with a nectar-white radiance and brilliant pure rays,
the lotus-face of the beloved, the exceedingly fragrant sandalwood dust,

children.text: srajo hṛdyāmodās tad idam akhilaṃ rāgiṇi jane
children.translated_text: garlands of heart-pleasing fragrance — all this causes inner turmoil in the passionate person,

children.text: karoty antaḥ kṣobhaṃ na tu viṣaya-saṃsarga-vimukhe || BharSt_2.89 ||
children.translated_text: but not in one who has turned away from sense-objects. (BharSt_2.89)
The rainy season, inflaming desire with the appearance of young women,
fragrant with blossoming <s>jātī</s> flowers,
heavy with the weight of high, full breasts —

children.text: prāvṛṭ tanute kasya na harṣam || BharSt_2.90 ||
children.translated_text: to whom does it not bring delight? (BharSt_2.90)
The sky filled with clouds, the earth covered with <s>kandalī</s> plants,
the breezes fragrant with fresh <s>kuṭaja</s> and <s>kadamba</s> blossoms,
the forest glades delightful with the sweet cries of peacock flocks —

children.text: sukhinam asukhinaṃ vā sarvam utkaṇṭhayanti || BharSt_2.91 ||
children.translated_text: all these fill both the happy and the unhappy with longing. (BharSt_2.91)
Above, a dense mass of clouds,
on all sides, mountains with dancing peacocks,
the earth white with <s>kandalī</s> flowers —
where shall the traveler cast his gaze? (BharSt_2.92)
On this side, the flashing of lightning vines; on that, the wafting fragrance of the <s>ketakī</s> tree;
from here, the rumbling thunder of rising rain-clouds;
from there, the melodious cries of sporting peacocks — for those long-lashed women,

children.text: kathaṃ yāsyanty ete viraha-divasāḥ sambhṛta-rasāḥ || BharSt_2.93 ||
children.translated_text: how will these days of separation, so rich with sentiment, pass? (BharSt_2.93)
When in the sky, dark beyond the passage of even a needle, with the thunder of full rain-clouds,
I think wisely, and clusters of raindrops fall,
this golden and captivating flash of lightning

children.text: mudaṃ ca mlāniṃ ca prathayati pathi svaira-sudṛśām || BharSt_2.94 ||
children.translated_text: produces both delight and dejection in the free-gazing women on the road. (BharSt_2.94)

children.text: āsāreṇa na harmyataḥ priyatamair yātuṃ bahiḥ śakyate
children.translated_text: Because of the downpour, the beloved cannot go out from the mansion;
trembling with cold, the large-eyed one clings tightly;
the breezes, cool with spray, have become supreme relievers of exhaustion —

children.text: dhanyānāṃ bata durdinaṃ sudinatāṃ yāti priyā-saṅgame || BharSt_2.95 ||
children.translated_text: for the fortunate, a stormy day attains the quality of a fine day in the company of the beloved! (BharSt_2.95)
Having slept through half the night, limbs slack and weary from the exertion of passionate lovemaking, unbearable
thirst having arisen, devoted to the intoxication of wine, on a secluded rooftop terrace,
freed from the loose creeper-arms of the beloved exhausted by love's enjoyment, with parched throat —

children.text: jyotsnābhinnāccha-dhāraṃ pibati na salilaṃ śāradaṃ manda-puṇyaḥ || BharSt_2.96 ||
children.translated_text: does not the man of little merit drink the autumn water, with its clear stream split by moonlight? (BharSt_2.96)
In winter, eating curds, milk, ghee, and rice, clad in madder-dyed garments,
bodies thickly anointed with saffron paste, cut off from the world by splendid lovemaking,
embraced by beloved women with round thighs and full breasts, within the house,
mouths filled with betel leaf and areca nut — the fortunate sleep in bliss! (BharSt_2.97)
In the season when the radiant <s>priyangu</s> flowers bloom, when bees swarm drunkenly around blossoming <s>kunda</s> flowers,
when the noble splendor of <s>mandāra</s> trees sways in the frosty breeze,

children.text: yeṣāṃ no kaṇṭha-lagnā kṣaṇam api tuhina-kṣoda-dakṣā mṛgākṣī
children.translated_text: for those young men around whose necks a doe-eyed woman skilled at dispelling the frost's bite does not cling even for a moment,

children.text: tesām āyāma-yāmā yama-sadana-samā yāminī yāti yūnām || BharSt_2.98 ||
children.translated_text: the winter nights, long as ages, pass like the abode of <s>Yama</s> (Death). (BharSt_2.98)

children.text: cumbanto gaṇḍa-bhittīr alakavati mukhe sītkṛtāny ādadhānā
children.translated_text: Kissing their cheeks, eliciting sighs upon their faces framed by curls,
causing the full breasts to bristle with goosebumps beneath their bodices,
making the thighs tremble, causing garments to slip from their broad hips —

children.text: vyaktaṃ kāntā-janānāṃ viṭa-carita-bhṛtaḥ śaiśirā vānti vātāḥ || BharSt_2.99 ||
children.translated_text: clearly, the wintry winds blow upon the bodies of beloved women like practiced libertines! (BharSt_2.99)

children.text: keśānākulayan dṛśo mukulayan vāso balād ākṣipannātanvan
children.translated_text: Disheveling the hair, half-closing the eyes, forcibly pulling at the garments,
producing goosebumps, gradually revealing trembling from excitement,
again and again pressing the lips with noble, loud sighs —

children.text: prāyaḥ śaiśira eṣa samprati marut kāntāsu kāntāyate || BharSt_2.100 ||
children.translated_text: this wintry wind, it seems, now acts as a lover to the beloved women. (BharSt_2.100)

children.text: yady asya nāsti ruciraṃ tasmiṃs tasya spṛhā manojñe 'pi |
children.translated_text: If she has no delight in him, she has no desire even for what is charming in him;

children.text: ramaṇīye 'pi sudhāṃśau na manaḥ-kāmaḥ sarojinyāḥ || BharSt_2.101 ||
children.translated_text: even for the delightful moon, the lotus-pool has no heart's desire. (BharSt_2.101)

children.text: vairāgye saṃcaraty eko nītau bhramati cāparaḥ |
children.translated_text: One person moves in renunciation, another wanders in polity,

children.text: śṛṅgāre ramate kaścid bhuvi bhedāḥ parasparam || BharSt_2.102 ||
children.translated_text: yet another delights in love — on earth, people differ from one another. (BharSt_2.102)
Thus may there be auspiciousness!
Adorned on his crest with the beautiful crescent moon bud, his radiant crest-flame blazing,
playfully having burnt the fluttering moth that is <s>Kāma</s> (Desire), shining at the forefront of the state of supreme good,
dispelling from within the heavy mass of darkness that is beginningless delusion,

children.text: śvetaḥ-sadmani yogināṃ vijayate jñāna-pradīpo haraḥ || BharSt_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: in the pure abode of <s>yogins</s>, the lamp of knowledge that is <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) triumphs! (BharSt_3.1)

<s>Vairāgya-Śataka</s> (Century on Renunciation)
by <s>Bhartṛhari</s>

children.text: bhrāntaṃ deśam aneka-durga-viṣamaṃ prāptaṃ na kiñcit phalaṃ
children.translated_text: I have wandered through many lands, difficult and treacherous, and gained nothing;

children.text: tyaktvā jāti-kulābhimānam ucitaṃ sevā kṛtā niṣphalā |
children.translated_text: abandoning the pride of birth and family, I performed servile attendance — all in vain.
I have eaten, stripped of dignity, in the houses of others, wary as a crow —

children.text: tṛṣṇe jṛmbhasi pāpa-karma-piśune nādyāpi santuṣyasi || BharSt_3.2 ||
children.translated_text: O Craving, you vile instigator of sinful deeds, still you yawn and stretch, still you are not satisfied! (BharSt_3.2)

children.text: utkhātaṃ nidhi-śaṅkayā kṣiti-talaṃ dhmātā girer dhātavo
children.translated_text: The surface of the earth has been dug up in hope of finding treasure; the ores of mountains have been smelted;

children.text: nistīrṇaḥ saritāṃ patir nṛpatayo yatnena santoṣitāḥ |
children.translated_text: the lord of rivers has been crossed; kings have been painstakingly gratified;
nights have been spent in cremation grounds by a mind devoted to the worship of <s>mantras</s> —

children.text: prāptaḥ kāṇa-varāṭako 'pi na mayā tṛṣṇe sakāmā bhava || BharSt_3.3 ||
children.translated_text: yet not even a broken cowrie shell has been obtained by me! O Craving, be satisfied! (BharSt_3.3)
The insults of the wicked have been endured; by those devoted to pleasing them, suppressing
inner tears, even smiling though the mind was empty;
salutations have been made even to those whose intelligence is blocked by the pillar of wealth —

children.text: tvam āśe moghāśe kima aparam ato nartayasi mām || BharSt_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: O Hope, O futile Hope, what further dance will you make me perform? (BharSt_3.4)
For the sake of these lives, as fleeting as a drop of water on a lotus petal,
what have we not resolved to do, having lost all discrimination?
Before the wealthy, whose minds are rendered senseless by the pride of riches,
Enough of shame at recounting one's own virtues, which itself is a downfall. || BharSt_3.5 ||

children.text: kṣāntaṃ na kṣamayā gṛhocita-sukhaṃ tyaktaṃ na santoṣataḥ
children.translated_text: We endured, but not out of forbearance; we abandoned the comforts of household life, but not from contentment;
we bore the unbearable afflictions of cold, heat, and wind, but it was not <s>tapas</s> (austerity) performed;

children.text: dhyātaṃ vittam ahar-niśaṃ nityamita-prāṇair na śambhoḥ padaṃ
children.translated_text: we meditated day and night, but on wealth — not on the feet of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), with our very life-breath;

children.text: tat-tat-karma kṛtaṃ yad eva munibhis tais taiḥ phalair vañcitāḥ || BharSt_3.6 ||
children.translated_text: we performed all those very deeds that the sages perform, yet we were cheated of all their fruits. || BharSt_3.6 ||

children.text: bhogā na bhuktā vayam eva bhuktās
children.translated_text: Pleasures were not enjoyed by us — rather, we ourselves were consumed by them;

children.text: tapo na taptaṃ vayam eva taptāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>tapas</s> (austerity) was not performed by us — rather, we ourselves were scorched;

children.text: kālo na yāto vayam eva yātāstṛṣṇā
children.translated_text: time did not pass away — rather, we ourselves have passed away; desire

children.text: na jīrṇā vayam eva jīrṇāḥ || BharSt_3.7 ||
children.translated_text: has not grown old — rather, we ourselves have grown old. || BharSt_3.7 ||
The face is invaded by wrinkles, the head is marked with grey hair;
the limbs grow feeble — desire alone remains youthful. || BharSt_3.8 ||
When discrimination expands and the mind becomes calm, desire subsides;
but when it ripens in the lofty embrace of passion, it spreads all the more;
pitiable is one who is seized by the devouring depths of wealth decayed by old age — a vessel of desire,

children.text: yasyāṃ bhavati marutām apy adhipatiḥ || BharSt_3.8*1 ||
children.translated_text: in which even the lord of the <s>Maruts</s> (wind gods) becomes ensnared. || BharSt_3.8*1 ||
The desire for pleasures has ceased, honor among men has also faded,
friends equal in age have all departed to heaven;

children.text: śanair yaṣṭy utthānaṃ ghana-timira-ruddhe ca nayane
children.translated_text: rising is only possible with the aid of a staff, and the eyes are obstructed by dense darkness —

children.text: aho mūḍhaḥ kāyas tad api maraṇāpāya-cakitaḥ || BharSt_3.9 ||
children.translated_text: alas, this foolish body is still terrified at the approach of death! || BharSt_3.9 ||
Hope is a river, with the waters of fantasy, agitated by waves of craving,
infested with crocodiles of passion, with birds of speculation, destroying the trees of fortitude;
exceedingly difficult to cross with its whirlpools of delusion, with towering banks of anxiety —

children.text: tasyāḥ para-gatā viśuddham alaso nandanti yogīśvarāḥ || BharSt_3.10 ||
children.translated_text: those great <s>yogīśvaras</s> (masters of yoga) who have reached its far shore rejoice in purity. || BharSt_3.10 ||
I do not see any good conduct arising from <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence);

children.text: vipākaḥ puṇyānāṃ janayati bhayaṃ me vimṛśataḥ |
children.translated_text: the ripening of merits, when I reflect upon it, fills me with fear;
for sense objects, long cultivated through great heaps of merit,

children.text: mahānto jāyante vyasanam iva dātuṃ viṣayiṇām || BharSt_3.11 ||
children.translated_text: grow mighty, as if to bring calamity upon those attached to them. || BharSt_3.11 ||
Sense objects, even when enjoyed for the longest time, must inevitably depart;

children.text: viyoge ko bhedas tyajati na jano yat svayam amūn |
children.translated_text: what difference is there in separation, since people do not abandon them of their own accord?
Departing on their own, they cause incomparable torment to the mind;

children.text: svayaṃ tyaktā hy ete śama-sukham anantaṃ vidadhati || BharSt_3.12 ||
children.translated_text: but when abandoned voluntarily, they bestow infinite peace and happiness. || BharSt_3.12 ||
Those whose intellects are purified by the discrimination of <s>Brahman</s>-knowledge perform what is truly difficult,

children.text: yan muñcanty upabhoga-bhāñjy api dhanāny ekāntato niḥspṛhāḥ |
children.translated_text: for, completely desireless, they renounce even wealth that could furnish enjoyments;

children.text: samprātān na purā na samprati na ca prāptau dṛḍha-pratyayān
children.translated_text: yet we, who neither possessed them before, nor possess them now, nor have firm expectation of obtaining them,

children.text: vāñchā-mātra-parigrahān api paraṃ tyaktuṃ na śaktā vayam || BharSt_3.13 ||
children.translated_text: are unable to renounce even the mere grasping after desires. || BharSt_3.13 ||

children.text: dhanyānāṃ giri-kandareṣu vasatāṃ jyotiḥ paraṃ dhyāyatāmānandāśru-
children.translated_text: Blessed are those who dwell in mountain caves, meditating on the supreme light — the birds
drink the water of their tears of bliss and sleep fearlessly in their laps;
but our lives are wasted in the amusements of palaces, pools, and pleasure gardens
fashioned by our own fantasies. || BharSt_3.14 ||
Food obtained by begging, and that too tasteless and taken only once a day;
the earth for a bed, and one's own body the only attendant;
a patched quilt of a hundred worn-out fragments for clothing —

children.text: hā hā tathāpi viṣayā na parityajanti || BharSt_3.15 ||
children.translated_text: alas, alas! Even so, sense pleasures do not abandon us! || BharSt_3.15 ||
The breasts are but knots of flesh, yet they are compared to golden pitchers;

children.text: mukhaṃ śleṣmāgāraṃ tad api ca śaśāṅkena tulitam |
children.translated_text: the face is a storehouse of phlegm, yet it is likened to the moon;
the hips, dripping with urine, rival the head of a great elephant —

children.text: muhur nindyaṃ rūpaṃ kavi-jana-viśeṣair guru-kṛtam || BharSt_3.16 ||
children.translated_text: this form, which deserves constant censure, is exalted by the special art of poets. || BharSt_3.16 ||
Among the passionate, <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) alone excels, who took his beloved as half his body;

children.text: nīrāgeṣu jano vimukta-lalanāsaṅgo na yasmāt paraḥ |
children.translated_text: among the passionless, there is no one superior to him, for he is free from all attachment to women;
the rest of the world, bewildered and bitten by the serpent-venom of irresistible <s>Smara</s>'s (Kāma's) arrows,

children.text: śeṣaḥ kāma-viḍambitān na viṣayān bhoktuṃ na moktuṃ kṣamaḥ || BharSt_3.17 ||
children.translated_text: can neither enjoy nor renounce the sense objects that <s>Kāma</s> (desire) mocks them with. || BharSt_3.17 ||
Let the moth, not knowing the nature of burning, fall into the fierce flame;

children.text: sa mīno 'py ajñānād baḍiśa-yutam aśnātu piśitam |
children.translated_text: let the fish, out of ignorance, swallow the bait along with the hook;

children.text: vijānanto 'py ete vayam iha viyaj jāla-jaṭilān
children.translated_text: but we, though fully knowing, do not release the tangled snares of passion —

children.text: na muñcāmaḥ kānām ahaha gahano moha-mahimā || BharSt_3.18 ||
children.translated_text: alas, how profound is the power of delusion! || BharSt_3.18 ||

children.text: tṛṣā śuṣyaty āsye pibati salilaṃ śīta-madhuraṃ
children.translated_text: When the mouth is parched with thirst, one drinks cool, sweet water;
when tormented by hunger, one devours rice mixed with meat and the like;
when the fire of desire is blazing, one embraces a woman all the more tightly —

children.text: pratīkāraṃ vyādhaḥ sukham iti viparyasyati janaḥ || BharSt_3.19 ||
children.translated_text: people perversely call the mere treatment of disease "pleasure." || BharSt_3.19 ||

children.text: tuṅgaṃ veśma sutāḥ satām abhimatāḥ saṅkhyātigāḥ sampadaḥ
children.translated_text: A lofty mansion, sons esteemed by the virtuous, immeasurable riches,

children.text: kalyāṇī dayitā vayaś ca navam ity ajñāna-mūḍho janaḥ |
children.translated_text: a virtuous wife, and youth still fresh — the ignorant, deluded,
thinking this world to be imperishable, settle into the prison-house of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence);

children.text: saṃdṛśya kṣaṇa-bhaṅguraṃ tad akhilaṃ dhanyas tu sannyasyati || BharSt_3.20 ||
children.translated_text: but the blessed one, seeing all this to be momentary, renounces it. || BharSt_3.20 ||
Wretched, with wretched-faced little children always tugging at her worn-out garment,

children.text: krośadbhiḥ kṣudhitair niranna-vidhurā dṛśyā na ced gehinī |
children.translated_text: crying from hunger, destitute of food — if such is the sight of one's wife,
with voice choked and syllables broken and dissolved from fear of the refusal of his begging,

children.text: ko dehīti vadet sva-dagdha-jaṭharasyārthe manasvī pumān || BharSt_3.21 ||
children.translated_text: what self-respecting man would say "Give!" for the sake of his own accursed belly? || BharSt_3.21 ||
Most adept at cutting the knot of cherished great pride,
a brilliant moonlight that does not partake of the abundance of weighty virtues,
an axe to the spreading canopy of the vast creeper of modesty —
this pot of a belly, impossible to fill, makes a mockery of us. || BharSt_3.22 ||

children.text: puṇye grāme vane vā mahati sita-paṭac-channa-pālī kapāliṃ
children.translated_text: In a holy village or a great forest, carrying a bowl covered with a white cloth,
near the smoke-grey vicinity of the sacred fire fed by twice-born householders whose offerings are righteous,

children.text: dvāraṃ dvāraṃ praviṣṭo varam udara-darī-pūraṇāya kṣudhārto
children.translated_text: entering door after door, hungry, to fill the cavity of the belly —

children.text: mānī prāṇaiḥ sanātho na punar anudinaṃ tulya-kulyesu dīnaḥ || BharSt_3.23 ||
children.translated_text: it is better to live with self-respect and dignity, than to be wretched day after day among one's equals. || BharSt_3.23 ||
Have the places on <s>Himavat</s> (the Himalayas), cooled by the spray of drops from the waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
with beautiful rock surfaces inhabited by <s>Vidyādharas</s> (celestial beings),
perished, that
people delight in the food of others received with contempt? || BharSt_3.24 ||

children.text: kiṃ kandāḥ kandarebhyaḥ pralayam upagatā nirjharā vā giribhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Have the roots from the caves perished? Have the mountain streams dried up?

children.text: pradhvastā vā tarubhyaḥ sarasa-gala-bhṛto valkalinyaś ca śākhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Have the trees been destroyed, along with their branches bearing juicy bark garments?

children.text: vīkṣyante yan mukhāni prasabham apagata-praśrayāṇāṃ khalānāṃ
children.translated_text: That people must behold the faces of the wicked, devoid of all courtesy,
whose brow-creepers dance in the wind of pride born from their meager wealth gained with difficulty? || BharSt_3.25 ||

children.text: puṇyair mūla-phalais tathā praṇayinīṃ vṛttiṃ kuruṣvādhunā
children.translated_text: Now live on the holy roots and fruits, maintaining a loving livelihood;

children.text: bhū-śayyāṃ nava-pallavair akṛpaṇair uttiṣṭha yāvo vanam |
children.translated_text: spread your bed of fresh shoots without miserliness — arise, let us go to the forest!
Where the very name is not heard of those petty lords
whose undiscriminating, deluded minds produce speech bewildered by the disease and corruption of wealth. || BharSt_3.26 ||
Fruit is freely obtained without effort from every tree in every forest;
cool, sweet water from holy rivers at every turn;
a bed of soft and lovely creeper-shoots for a soft touch —

children.text: sahante santāpaṃ tad api dhanināṃ dvāri kṛpaṇāḥ || BharSt_3.27 ||
children.translated_text: yet the wretched still endure the heat at the doors of the wealthy! || BharSt_3.27 ||
Those who stand before wealthy men, sharing in the misery of supplication,
and those who hold in low esteem the intellect that is satisfied by the rejection of sense objects —
I would recall their days with inner, suppressed laughter,
while seated on a rocky bed in a mountain cave, during a pause in meditation. || BharSt_3.28 ||

children.text: ye santoṣa-nirantara-pramuditas teṣāṃ na bhinnā mudo
children.translated_text: Those who are constantly delighted by contentment — their joy is unbroken;

children.text: ye tv anye dhana-lubdha-saṅkala-dhiyas tesāṃ na tṛṣṇāhatā |
children.translated_text: but those others whose minds are fettered by greed for wealth — their craving is never quenched;

children.text: itthaṃ kasya kṛte kutaḥ sa vidhinā kīdṛk-padaṃ sampadāṃ
children.translated_text: thus, for whose sake, from what source, and to what state of prosperity has fate ordained?

children.text: svātmany eva samāpta-hema-mahimā merur na me rocate || BharSt_3.29 ||
children.translated_text: Even <s>Meru</s>, in whom the glory of gold is self-contained, does not please me. || BharSt_3.29 ||
Food obtained by begging — free from humiliation, without reciprocal obligation, dispelling fear from all sides,
crushing envy, pride, and arrogance, destroying the flood of sorrows,
everywhere and every day easily obtained without effort, dear to the virtuous, purifying —

children.text: śambhoḥ satram avāyam akṣaya-nidhiṃ śaṃsanti yogīśvarāḥ || BharSt_3.30 ||
children.translated_text: the great <s>yogīśvaras</s> (masters of yoga) praise it as the perpetual feast of <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), an inexhaustible treasure. || BharSt_3.30 ||

children.text: bhoge rogamayaṃ kule cyuti-bhayaṃ vitte nṛpālād bhayaṃ
children.translated_text: In enjoyment there is disease; in family, fear of decline; in wealth, fear of the king;

children.text: māne dhainya-bhayaṃ bale ripu-bhayaṃ rūpe jarāya bhayam |
children.translated_text: in honor, fear of humiliation; in strength, fear of enemies; in beauty, fear of old age;

children.text: śāstre vādibhayaṃ guṇe khala-bhayaṃ kāye kṛtāntād bhayaṃ
children.translated_text: in learning, fear of disputants; in virtue, fear of the wicked; in the body, fear of death —

children.text: sarvaṃ vastu bhayānvitaṃ bhuvi nṝṇāṃ vairāgyam evābhayam || BharSt_3.31 ||
children.translated_text: everything in this world is attended by fear; <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) alone is fearless. || BharSt_3.31 ||

children.text: ākrāntaṃ maraṇena janma jarasā cātyujjvalaṃ yauvanaṃ
children.translated_text: Birth is assailed by death, and radiant youth by old age;
contentment by the craving for wealth, and peace by the allurements of passionate women;

children.text: lokair matsaribhir guṇā vana-bhuvo vyālair nṛpā durjanair
children.translated_text: virtues by envious people, forests by serpents, kings by the wicked;

children.text: asthairyeṇa vibhūtayo 'py apahatā grastaṃ na kiṃ kena vā || BharSt_3.32 ||
children.translated_text: even prosperity is destroyed by inconstancy — what indeed is not devoured by something? || BharSt_3.32 ||
People's health is uprooted by hundreds of mental and physical afflictions;

children.text: lakṣmīr yatra patanti tatra vivṛta-dvārā iva vyāpadaḥ |
children.translated_text: wherever fortune alights, there calamities stand as if with open doors;

children.text: jātaṃ jātam avaśyam āśu vivaśaṃ mṛtyuḥ karoty ātmasāt
children.translated_text: whatever is born, death inevitably and swiftly makes its own;

children.text: tat kiṃ tena niraṅkuśena vidhinā yan nirmitaṃ susthiram || BharSt_3.33 ||
children.translated_text: then what has that unrestrained Fate created that is truly enduring? || BharSt_3.33 ||
Pleasures are as fleeting as the breaking of towering waves; life-breaths perish in an instant;

children.text: stokāny eva dināni yauvana-sukhaṃ sphūrtiḥ priyāsu sthitā |
children.translated_text: the days of youthful happiness are but few; ardor for loved ones is transient —

children.text: tat-saṃsāram asāram eva nikhilaṃ buddhvā budhā bodhakā
children.translated_text: therefore, knowing this entire <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) to be devoid of essence, the wise who are awakened,
should fix their minds on effort with a disposition gracious toward the welfare of the world. || BharSt_3.34 ||
Pleasures are as fickle as lightning flashing amidst a canopy of clouds;
life is as fragile as water clinging to lotus petals scattered by the wind;

children.text: līlā yauvana-lālasās tanubhṛtām ity ākalayya drutaṃ
children.translated_text: the playful passions of youth in embodied beings are fleeting — knowing this, swiftly

children.text: yoge dhairya-samādhi-siddhi-sulabhe buddhiṃ vidadhvaṃ budhāḥ || BharSt_3.35 ||
children.translated_text: fix your intellect, O wise ones, on <s>yoga</s>, which is easily attained through steadfastness and <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption). || BharSt_3.35 ||
Life is as unsteady as waves; the glory of youth lasts but a few days;
wealth is as fanciful as a wish; the host of pleasures is like the flickering of lightning in the rainy season;

children.text: kaṇṭhāśleṣopagūḍha tad api ca na ciraṃ yat priyābhaḥ praṇītaṃ
children.translated_text: even the embrace of a beloved held close to one's throat does not last long —

children.text: brahmaṇy āsakta-cittā bhavata bhavamayāmbhodhi-pāraṃ tarītum || BharSt_3.36 ||
children.translated_text: let your minds be devoted to <s>Brahman</s>, so as to cross the ocean of <s>bhava</s> (worldly existence)! || BharSt_3.36 ||
With difficulty one remains in the womb, confined in the midst of impurity with a constricted body;
in youth, enjoyment is marred by the agony of separation from one's beloved;
old age is a dwelling of the disdainful laughter of lovely-eyed women, and is otherwise also wretched —

children.text: saṃsāre re manuṣyā vadata yadi sukhaṃ svalpam apy asti kiñcit || BharSt_3.37 ||
children.translated_text: O people, tell me if there is even the slightest happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence)! || BharSt_3.37 ||
Old age stands like a tigress, threatening;

children.text: rogāś ca śatrava iva praharanti deham |
children.translated_text: diseases strike the body like enemies;
life flows away like water from a broken pot —

children.text: lokas tathāpy ahitam ācaratīti citram || BharSt_3.38 ||
children.translated_text: and yet the world still pursues what is harmful — how wondrous! || BharSt_3.38 ||

children.text: bhogā bhaṅgura-vṛttayo bahuvidhās tair eva cāyaṃ bhavastat
children.translated_text: Pleasures are of fickle nature and manifold, and by them alone this <s>bhava</s> (worldly existence) persists —

children.text: kasyeha kṛte paribhramata re lokāḥ kṛtaṃ ceṣṭataiḥ |
children.translated_text: for whose sake then do you wander, O people? Enough of striving for them!
Let the mind be composed in the pure cessation of the hundred snares of hope;

children.text: kāmotpatti-vaśāt svadhāmani yadi śraddeyam asmad-vacaḥ || BharSt_3.39 ||
children.translated_text: in its own abode, through the mastery over the arising of desire — if our words are to be believed. || BharSt_3.39 ||
O friend, blessed are those few who have severed the entanglements of the bonds of <s>bhava</s> (existence),
who in the forest have gone beyond the poison of sense objects, the venom within the mind;
they pass the night, beautiful with the expanse of the sky whitened by the light of the autumn moon,
their sole refuge being the contemplation of accumulated merit. || BharSt_3.39*1 ||
Where one who is established regards <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the hosts of <s>Maruts</s> as mere blades of grass,
by the taste of which the splendors of the sovereignty of the three worlds become insipid —

children.text: bhogaḥ ko 'pi sa eva eka paramo nityodito jṛmbhate
children.translated_text: There is some supreme enjoyment, one and unique, that ever rises and expands —

children.text: bhoḥ sādho kṣaṇa-bhaṅgure tad itare bhoge ratiṃ mā kṛthāḥ || BharSt_3.40 ||
children.translated_text: O good sir, do not take delight in those other pleasures that perish in an instant! || BharSt_3.40 ||

children.text: sā ramyā nagarī mahān sa nṛpatiḥ sāmanta-cakraṃ ca tat
children.translated_text: That was a lovely city, that was a great king, that was a circle of feudatories,

children.text: pārśve tasya ca sā vidagdha-pariṣat tāś candra-bimbānanāḥ |
children.translated_text: by his side was that assembly of the learned, and those were the moon-faced women;

children.text: udvṛttaḥ sa rāja-putra-nivahas te vandinas tāḥ kathāḥ
children.translated_text: that was the throng of proud princes, those were the bards, those were the tales —

children.text: sarvaṃ yasya vaśād agāt smṛti-pathaṃ kālāya tasmai namaḥ || BharSt_3.41 ||
children.translated_text: all that has passed into the realm of memory by whose power — to that <s>Kāla</s> (Time), salutation! || BharSt_3.41 ||

children.text: yatrānekaḥ kvacid api gṛhe tatra tiṣṭhaty athaiko
children.translated_text: Where many once dwelt in a certain house, there remains but one;

children.text: yatrāpy ekas tad anu bahavas tatra naiko 'pi cānte |
children.translated_text: where even one remained, thereafter many come, and at the end not even one;

children.text: itthaṃ nayau rajani-divasau lolayan dvāv ivākṣau
children.translated_text: thus, rolling night and day like two dice,

children.text: kālaḥ kalyo bhuvana-phalake kraḍati prāṇi-śāraiḥ || BharSt_3.42 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāla</s> (Time), the skilled player, plays upon the board of the world with living beings as game-pieces. || BharSt_3.42 ||
By the comings and goings of the sun, life is diminished day by day;
amid affairs weighty with the burden of many tasks, even time itself goes unnoticed;
seeing birth, old age, calamity, and death, no fear arises —

children.text: pītvā mohamayīṃ pramāda-madirām unmatta-bhūtaṃ jagat || BharSt_3.43 ||
children.translated_text: having drunk the wine of heedlessness, brewed of delusion, the world has become mad! || BharSt_3.43 ||

children.text: rātriḥ saiva punaḥ sa eva divaso matvā mudhā jantavo
children.translated_text: It is the same night again, the same day again — thinking them worthless, yet creatures
run about busily, engrossed in the very same endeavors commenced in secret;
by occupations whose objects are but repetitions, in this manner, by this fate,

children.text: saṃsāreṇa kadarthitā vayam aho mohān na lajjāmahe || BharSt_3.44 ||
children.translated_text: we are tormented by <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — alas, out of delusion we feel no shame! || BharSt_3.44 ||

children.text: na dhyānaṃ padam īśvarasya vidhivat saṃsāra-vicchittaye
children.translated_text: No meditation on the state of the Lord has been properly performed for the severing of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence);
<s>dharma</s> (righteous merit), skilled at bursting open the door-panels of heaven's gate, has not been acquired;
not even in a dream have we embraced the full breasts and thighs of a woman —

children.text: mātuḥ kevalam eva yauvana-vana-cchede kuṭhārā vayam || BharSt_3.45 ||
children.translated_text: we are merely axes for cutting down the youthful forest of our mother! || BharSt_3.45 ||
Learning fit for the cultured, capable of subduing hosts of opponents, has not been mastered;

children.text: khaḍgāgraiḥ kari-kumbha-pīṭha-dalanair nākaṃ na nītaṃ yaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: fame has not been raised to heaven by the splitting of elephants' frontal globes with sword-points;
the nectar of a beloved's tender sprout-like lip has not been tasted at moonrise —

children.text: tāruṇyaṃ gatam eva niṣphalam aho śūnyālaye dīpavat || BharSt_3.46 ||
children.translated_text: youth has passed away fruitlessly, alas, like a lamp in an empty house! || BharSt_3.46 ||

children.text: vidyā nādhigatā kalaṅka-rahitā vittaṃ ca nopārjitaṃ
children.translated_text: Learning free from blemish has not been acquired, nor has wealth been earned;

children.text: śuśrūṣāpi samāhitena manasā pitror na sampāditā |
children.translated_text: nor has devoted service to parents been rendered with a concentrated mind;
beloveds with wide trembling eyes have not been embraced even in dreams —

children.text: kālo 'yaṃ para-piṇḍa-lolupatayā kākair iva preryate || BharSt_3.47 ||
children.translated_text: this lifetime is driven along like crows, out of greed for another's morsel of food. || BharSt_3.47 ||

children.text: vayaṃ yebhyo jātāś cira-parigatā eva khalu te
children.translated_text: Those from whom we were born have long since departed;

children.text: samaṃ yaiḥ saṃvṛddhāḥ smṛti-viṣayatāṃ te 'pi gamitāḥ |
children.translated_text: those with whom we grew up have also passed into the realm of memory;
now we too stand here, on the verge of falling each day,
having reached the same condition as trees on the sandy bank of a river. || BharSt_3.48 ||

children.text: āyur varṣa-śataṃ nṝṇāṃ parimitaṃ rātrau tad-ardhaṃ gataṃ
children.translated_text: The lifespan of men is limited to a hundred years; half of that is gone in sleep at night;
of the remaining half, again half is lost in childhood and old age;
the rest is spent in service and the like, accompanied by illness, separation, and sorrow —

children.text: jīve vārita-raṅga-cañcalatare saukhyaṃ kutaḥ prāṇinām || BharSt_3.49 ||
children.translated_text: in this life, more fickle than a ripple on water, whence comes happiness for living beings? || BharSt_3.49 ||

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ bālo bhūtvā kṣaṇam pai yuvā kāma-rasikaḥ
children.translated_text: For a moment one is a child, for a moment a youth delighting in love,

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ vittair hīnaḥ kṣaṇam api ca sampūrṇa-vibhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: for a moment destitute of wealth, for a moment endowed with full prosperity;
then with limbs worn out by old age, his body adorned with wrinkles like an actor's makeup,
a man at the end of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) enters the city of <s>Yama</s> (the god of death). || BharSt_3.50 ||
You are a king; we too are exalted with pride in our wisdom acquired by serving great teachers;

children.text: khyātas tvaṃ vibhavair yaśāṃsi kavayo dikṣu pratanvanti naḥ |
children.translated_text: you are renowned for your wealth, while we poets spread our fame across the quarters;

children.text: itthaṃ māna-dhanāti-dūram ubhayor apy āvayor antaraṃ
children.translated_text: thus the distance between us both, rich in honor, is vast —

children.text: yady asmāsu parāṅmukho 'si vayam apy ekāntato niḥspṛhā || BharSt_3.51 ||
children.translated_text: if you turn your face away from us, we too are utterly without desire. || BharSt_3.51 ||

children.text: arthānām īśiṣe tvaṃ vayam api ca girām īśmahe yāvad arthaṃ
children.translated_text: You are the master of wealth, and we too are masters of speech to the extent needed;
you are a hero, while we have inexhaustible skill in subduing the pride of debaters;

children.text: sevante tvāṃ dhanāḍhyā matimalahatayemām api śrotu-kāmāmayy
children.translated_text: the wealthy serve you, while those who wish to hear serve us because of the purity of our intellect —

children.text: apy āsthā na te cet tvayi mama nitarām eva rājann anāsthā || BharSt_3.52 ||
children.translated_text: if you have no regard for us, then we, O king, have assuredly even less regard for you. || BharSt_3.52 ||

children.text: vayam iha parituṣṭā valkalais tvaṃ dukūlaiḥ
children.translated_text: We here are content with bark garments, you with fine silks —
the contentment is equal here, the difference is no difference at all;

children.text: sa tu bhavatu daridro yasya tṛṣṇā viśālā
children.translated_text: let him be called poor whose craving is vast —

children.text: manasi ca parituṣṭe ko 'rthavān ko daridraḥ || BharSt_3.53 ||
children.translated_text: when the mind is content, who is wealthy and who is poor? || BharSt_3.53 ||

children.text: phalam alam aśanāya svādu pānāya toyaṃ
children.translated_text: Fruit is sufficient for food, sweet water for drink,

children.text: kṣitir api śayanārthaṃ vāsase valkalaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: the earth itself for a bed, and bark for clothing;
I cannot bring myself to tolerate the insolence of wicked men
whose every sense is intoxicated by drinking the honey of fresh clouds. || BharSt_3.54 ||
Let us eat alms, let us wear the sky as our garment,

children.text: śayīmahi mahī-pṛṣṭhe kurvīmahi kim īśvaraiḥ || BharSt_3.55 ||
children.translated_text: let us sleep upon the surface of the earth — what have we to do with lords? || BharSt_3.55 ||

children.text: na naṭā nā viṭā na gāyakā na ca sabhyetara-vāda-cuñcavaḥ |
children.translated_text: We are not actors, nor jesters, nor singers, nor those clever at vulgar discourse;

children.text: nṛpam īkṣitum atra ke vayaṃ stana-bhārān amitā na yoṣitaḥ || BharSt_3.56 ||
children.translated_text: who are we to gaze upon a king? We are not women with boundless weight of breasts. || BharSt_3.56 ||

children.text: vipula-hṛdayair īśair etaj jagaj janitaṃ purā
children.translated_text: This world was created of old by lords of magnanimous heart,

children.text: vidhṛtam aparair dattaṃ cānyair vijitya tṛṇaṃ yathā |
children.translated_text: sustained by others, and given away by yet others, conquered as if it were a blade of grass;

children.text: iha hi bhuvanāny anyair dhīrāś caturdaśa bhuñjate
children.translated_text: here indeed other courageous ones enjoy the fourteen worlds —

children.text: katipaya-pura-svāmye puṃsāṃ ka eṣa mada-jvaraḥ || BharSt_3.57 ||
children.translated_text: what is this fever of pride in men over the lordship of a few cities? || BharSt_3.57 ||

children.text: abhuktāyāṃ yasyāṃ kṣaṇam api na yātaṃ nṛpa-śatair
children.translated_text: Of that earth which has not been enjoyed even for a moment by hundreds of kings,

children.text: dhuvas tasyā lābhe ka iva bahumānaḥ kṣiti-bhṛtām |
children.translated_text: what great esteem can there be for rulers who gain possession of her?
Over a fraction of a fraction of that, over a mere particle of her portion, they become lords,

children.text: viṣāde kartavye vidadhati jaḍāḥ pratyuta mudam || BharSt_3.58 ||
children.translated_text: and the foolish feel joy when grief is called for! || BharSt_3.58 ||

children.text: mṛt-piṇḍo jala-rekhayā bala-yatiḥ sarvo 'py ayaṃ nanv aṇuḥ
children.translated_text: This entire world is but a lump of clay, its boundaries mere lines drawn in water, all truly minute;

children.text: svāṃśīkṛtya sa eva saṅgara-śatai rājñāṃ gaṇā bhuñjate |
children.translated_text: yet hosts of kings, having claimed their own share, enjoy it through hundreds of battles;

children.text: ye dadyur dadato 'thavā kim aparaṃ kṣudrā daridraṃ bhṛśaṃ
children.translated_text: whether they give or whether they do not — what else are these petty ones but abjectly poor?

children.text: dhig dhik tān puruṣādhamān dhanakaṇān vāñchanti tebhyo 'pi ye || BharSt_3.59 ||
children.translated_text: Shame, shame on those lowest of men, and on those too who beg grains of wealth from them! || BharSt_3.59 ||

children.text: sa jātaḥ ko 'py āsīn madana-ripuṇā mūrdhni dhavalaṃ
children.translated_text: Someone was born — he by whom the enemy of <s>Madana</s> (Kāma), that is <s>Śiva</s>, has placed high upon his head
a white skull as an ornament;
now, because certain men, their minds intent on preserving their lives,

children.text: namadbhiḥ kaḥ puṃsām ayam atula-darpa-jvara-bharaḥ || BharSt_3.60 ||
children.translated_text: bow before him — what is this incomparable fever of pride among men? || BharSt_3.60 ||
Propitiating the minds of others in manifold ways day after day,

children.text: prasādaṃ kiṃ netuṃ viśasi hṛdaya kleśa-kalitam |
children.translated_text: O heart, why do you enter into seeking their favor, entwined with affliction?
When you are serene within, the host of wish-fulfilling gems (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) arises spontaneously —

children.text: viviktaḥ saṅkalpaḥ kim abhilaṣitaṃ puṣyati na te || BharSt_3.61 ||
children.translated_text: does not a pure resolve fulfill whatever is desired by you? || BharSt_3.61 ||

children.text: satyām eva trilokī-sariti hara-śiraś cumbinīvac chaṭāyāṃ
children.translated_text: While the river of the three worlds (the <s>Gaṅgā</s>) truly exists, kissing the head of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) with its currents,

children.text: sad-vṛttiṃ kalpayantyāṃ baṭa-viṭapa-bhavair valkalaiḥ sat-phalaiś ca |
children.translated_text: providing a virtuous livelihood through bark garments and good fruits from the banyan tree —
what wise man, if he did not feel compassion for his own family,

children.text: vaktraṃ vīkṣeta duḥsthe yadi hi na vibhṛyāt sve kuṭumbe 'nukampām || BharSt_3.61*1 ||
children.translated_text: would look upon the faces of those afflicted with the terrible sickness and sorrow born of the fever of misfortune? || BharSt_3.61*1 ||

children.text: paribhramasi kiṃ mudhā kvacana citta viśrāmyatāṃ
children.translated_text: O mind, why do you wander about in vain? Rest somewhere!

children.text: svayaṃ bhavati yad yathā bhavati tat tathā nānyathā |
children.translated_text: What happens of its own accord happens just so and not otherwise;
not recalling the past, and not imagining the future,
I experience pleasures that come unsought. || BharSt_3.62 ||
Therefore, turn away from this dense, toilsome jungle of sense objects, and take refuge in
the path of the highest good, skilled in the work of quenching all suffering, at once;

children.text: svātmībhāvam upaihi santyaja nijāṃ kallola-lolaṃ gatiṃ
children.translated_text: attain identity with the Self, abandon your own course that is restless with waves —

children.text: mā bhūyo bhaja bhaṅgurāṃ bhava-ratiṃ cetaḥ prasīdādhunā || BharSt_3.63 ||
children.translated_text: O mind, do not again embrace the fleeting pleasure of worldly existence; be serene now! || BharSt_3.63 ||

children.text: mohaṃ mārjaya tām upārjaya ratiṃ candrārdha-cūḍāmaṇau
children.translated_text: Wipe away delusion; cultivate devotion to the one whose crest-jewel is the half-moon (<s>Śiva</s>);
O mind, embrace attachment to the banks of the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>);

children.text: ko vā vīciṣu budbudeṣu ca taḍil-lekhāsu ca śrīṣu ca
children.translated_text: for what reliance can there be on waves, on bubbles, on flashes of lightning, on fortune,

children.text: jvālāgreṣu ca pannageṣu sarid-vegeṣu ca ca-pratyayaḥ || BharSt_3.64 ||
children.translated_text: on the tips of flames, on serpents, or on the currents of rivers? || BharSt_3.64 ||

children.text: cetaś cintaya mā ramāṃ sakṛd imām asthāyinīm āsthayā
children.translated_text: O mind, do not think of <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī, fortune) even once with attachment, for she is transient,
a courtesan whose trade is to dwell in the frowning brow-huts of kings;
having entered the doorways of houses wearing rags as our jacket, in the streets of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,
we shall await alms fallen into the bowl of our hands. || BharSt_3.65 ||
Before us, song; at our sides, eloquent poets from the south;
behind, the jingling of playful bracelets of the fan-bearing women —

children.text: yady asty evaṃ kuru bhava-rasāsvādane lampaṭatvaṃ
children.translated_text: if it be so, then be passionate in savoring the pleasures of worldly existence;

children.text: no cec cetaḥ praviśa sahasā nirvikalpe samādhau || BharSt_3.66 ||
children.translated_text: if not, O mind, enter at once into the thought-free <s>samādhi</s> (deep meditative absorption)! || BharSt_3.66 ||
Wealth fulfilling all desires has been obtained — then what?

children.text: nyastaṃ padaṃ śirasi vidviṣatāṃ tataḥ kim |
children.translated_text: The foot has been placed upon the heads of enemies — then what?
Friends have been gratified with riches — then what?

children.text: kalpaṃ sthitās tanubhṛtāṃ tanavas tataḥ kim || BharSt_3.67 ||
children.translated_text: The bodies of the embodied have endured for an aeon — then what? || BharSt_3.67 ||
Devotion to the Lord is present, the fear of death and rebirth is lodged in the heart,

children.text: sneho na bandhuṣu na manmathajā vikārāḥ |
children.translated_text: there is no attachment to kinsmen, nor the disturbances born of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love);
companionship is free from fault, victory belongs to the forest —

children.text: vairāgyam asti kim itaḥ paramarthanīyam || BharSt_3.68 ||
children.translated_text: <s>vairāgya</s> (renunciation) is here — what more is there to be desired beyond this? || BharSt_3.68 ||
Therefore, meditate upon that infinite, undecaying, supreme, effulgent

children.text: tad brahma cintaya kim ebhir asad-vikalpaiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> (the Absolute) — what use are these false imaginations?
Compared to which, sovereignty over these worlds and enjoyments and the like
are considered trivial by pitiable worldly people. || BharSt_3.69 ||
You descend to the netherworld, you ascend beyond the sky,
you roam the circle of the directions, O mind, with your fickleness;
yet even by wandering, how is it that you never arrive at the pure, self-contained

children.text: na brahma saṃsarasi virvṛtimm eṣi yena || BharSt_3.70 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>, by which you would attain liberation? || BharSt_3.70 ||

children.text: kiṃ vedaiḥ smṛtibhiḥ purāṇa-paṭhanaiḥ śāstrair mahā-vistaraiḥ
children.translated_text: What use are the <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Smṛtis</s>, the reading of the <s>Purāṇas</s>, the vast <s>Śāstras</s>,
or the bewildering ritual performances that yield the fruit of dwelling in the village-hut of heaven?
Except for that one thing — the fire at the end of time that destroys the structure of suffering in worldly existence —
the contemplation of entering the state of bliss of the Self — all the rest is mere merchant's trade! || BharSt_3.71 ||

children.text: nāyaṃ te samayo rahasyam adhunā nidrāti nātho yadi
children.translated_text: "This is not your time; the master is sleeping now; if

children.text: sthitvā drakṣyati kupyati prabhur iti dvāreṣu yeṣāṃ vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: you wait, he will see you; the lord will be angry" — at the doors of those at whose houses such words are spoken,

children.text: cetas tān apahāya yāhi bhavanaṃ devasya viśveśitur
children.translated_text: O mind, abandoning them, go to the abode of the God, the Lord of all,
where there is no doorkeeper, no harsh unkind words, and where supreme bliss is bestowed. || BharSt_3.71*1 ||
Since even the glorious <s>Meru</s> falls, engulfed in the fire at the end of an age,
and the oceans dry up, abodes of abundant crocodiles and sharks,

children.text: dharā gacchaty antaṃ dharaṇi-dhara-pādair api dhṛtā
children.translated_text: and the earth comes to an end, though upheld by the feet of the world-bearing mountains —
what talk can there be of this body, as fickle as the tip of a young elephant's ear? || BharSt_3.72 ||

children.text: gātraṃ saṅkucitaṃ gatir vigalitā bhraṣṭā ca dantāvalir
children.translated_text: The limbs have shriveled, the gait has faltered, the row of teeth has fallen out,

children.text: dṛṣṭir nakṣyati vardhate vadhiratā vaktraṃ ca lālāyate |
children.translated_text: sight is failing, deafness increases, the mouth drools;

children.text: vākyaṃ nādriyate ca bāndhava-jano bhāryā na śuśrūṣate
children.translated_text: one's words are heeded by no kinsman, one's wife no longer serves —

children.text: hā kaṣṭaṃ puruṣasya jīrṇa-vayasaḥ putro 'py amitrāyate || BharSt_3.73 ||
children.translated_text: alas, how bitter it is! For a man in decrepit old age, even his own son becomes an enemy! || BharSt_3.73 ||
Seeing the white color of the hair upon the head,
that abode of the humiliation of old age, then young women
avoid a man, departing far away
as from a <s>Caṇḍāla's</s> (outcaste's) well, mounted upon a frame of a hundred bones. || BharSt_3.74 ||

children.text: yāvat svastham idaṃ śarīram arujaṃ yāvac ca dūre jarā
children.translated_text: While this body is still healthy and free from disease, while old age is yet far off,

children.text: yāvac cendriya-śaktir apratihatā yāvat kṣayo nāyuṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: while the power of the senses is unimpaired, while life is not yet waning —

children.text: ātma-śreyasi tāvad eva viduṣā kāryaḥ prayatno mahān
children.translated_text: just then should the wise man make the greatest effort for the welfare of the Self;

children.text: sandīpte bhavane tu kūpa-khananaṃ pratyudyamaḥ kīdṛśaḥ || BharSt_3.75 ||
children.translated_text: for what use is digging a well when the house is already on fire? || BharSt_3.75 ||
The virtuous, practicing austerities — shall we dwell by the river of the gods (<s>Gaṅgā</s>)?
Shall we humbly attend to our wives, who are generous in virtues?
Or shall we drink the nectar-essence of varied poetry and floods of <s>śāstras</s>?

children.text: na vidmaḥ kiṃ kurmaḥ katipaya-nimeṣāyuṣi jane || BharSt_3.76 ||
children.translated_text: We do not know what to do, when human life lasts but a few eye-blinks. || BharSt_3.76 ||
These kings are hard to please, their minds fickle as horses;

children.text: vayaṃ tu sthūlecchāḥ sumahati phale baddha-manasaḥ |
children.translated_text: while we are coarse in our desires, our minds set on great rewards.

children.text: jarā dehaṃ mṛtyur harati dayitaṃ jīvitam idaṃ
children.translated_text: Old age carries away the body, death carries away this beloved life—

children.text: sakhe nānyac chreyo jagati viduṣe 'nyatra tapasaḥ || BharSt_3.77 ||
children.translated_text: O friend, there is no other good in the world for the wise, apart from austerity (<s>tapas</s>). || BharSt_3.77 ||

children.text: māne mlāyini khaṇḍite ca vasuni vyarthe prayāte 'rthini
children.translated_text: When honor has faded, wealth is broken, supplicants have gone away in vain,

children.text: kṣīṇe bandhu-jane gate parijane naṣṭe śanair yauvane |
children.translated_text: kinsmen are diminished, attendants have departed, youth has slowly vanished—

children.text: yuktaṃ kevalam etad eva sudhiyāṃ yaj jahnu-kanyā-payaḥpūtāgrāva-
children.translated_text: the only fitting course for the wise is dwelling somewhere in a grove on the slope of a cavern of the great mountain, whose rocks are purified by the waters of
<s>Jahnukanyā</s> (the Gaṅgā). || BharSt_3.78 ||
Delightful are the moonbeams; delightful is the grassy forest clearing;
delightful is the joy born from the company of the good; delightful are the tales in poetry;
delightful is the face of the beloved, trembling with tear-drops brought on by feigned anger—

children.text: sarvaṃ ramyam anityatām upagate citte na kiñcit punaḥ || BharSt_3.79 ||
children.translated_text: everything is delightful; but when the mind realizes impermanence, nothing is delightful anymore. || BharSt_3.79 ||

children.text: ramyaṃ harmya-talaṃ na kiṃ vasataye śravyaṃ na geyādikaṃ
children.translated_text: Is not the palace terrace delightful for dwelling? Is not song and the like pleasing to hear?
Does not the pleasure of union with one's beloved bring the greatest delight?
But perceiving all this to be as fleeting as the shadow of a lamp-flame flickering in the breeze from the wings of

children.text: cañcalam ākalayya sakalaṃ santo vanāntaṃ gatāḥ || BharSt_3.80 ||
children.translated_text: circling moths, the saintly ones have gone to the forest. || BharSt_3.80 ||

children.text: ā saṃsārāt tribhuvanam idaṃ cinvatāṃ tāt tādṛṅnaivāsmākaṃ
children.translated_text: Searching through this triple world from the beginning of <s>saṃsāra</s>, O father, nothing of that kind
has come within the path of our eyes or the range of our ears—
that which holds in check, with the sport of the tethering-post of self-restraint, the inner elephant of the mind,
intoxicated with deeply hidden pride, that elephant of sense-objects. || BharSt_3.81 ||

children.text: yad etat svacchandaṃ viharaṇam akārpaṇyam aśanaṃ
children.translated_text: This free wandering, this eating without wretchedness,
this dwelling with noble companions, this learning whose sole fruit is the vow of tranquility,

children.text: mano manda-spandaṃ bahir api cirasyāpi vimṛśanna
children.translated_text: the mind barely stirring, even when contemplating external things for a long time—

children.text: jāne kasyaiṣā pariṇatir udārasya tapasaḥ || BharSt_3.82 ||
children.translated_text: I do not know whose this is, this fruition of noble austerity (<s>tapas</s>). || BharSt_3.82 ||

children.text: jīrṇā eva manorathāś ca hṛdaye yātaṃ ca tad yauvanaṃ
children.translated_text: Desires have grown old indeed in the heart, that youth has departed;

children.text: hantāṅgeṣu guṇāś bandhya-phalatāṃ yātā guṇajñair vinā |
children.translated_text: alas, virtues in the limbs have reached barrenness without those who appreciate them.

children.text: kiṃ yuktaṃ sahasābhyupaiti balavān kālaḥ kṛtānto 'kṣamī
children.translated_text: What is the right course? Powerful, impatient Time, the Destroyer, approaches suddenly—

children.text: hā jñātaṃ madanāntakāṅghri-yugalaṃ muktvāsti nānyo gatiḥ || BharSt_3.83 ||
children.translated_text: ah, it is known: apart from the two feet of <s>Madanāntaka</s> (Śiva, the Destroyer of Kāma), there is no other refuge. || BharSt_3.83 ||
Whether in <s>Maheśvara</s>, the sovereign Lord of the worlds,
or in <s>Janārdana</s> (Viṣṇu), the inner soul of the universe—
I perceive no difference in essence;
yet my devotion is to Him who wears the crescent moon as a crest. || BharSt_3.84 ||
Seated comfortably on some riverbank whitened by the spreading splendor of moonlight,
on nights when darkness has been stilled, by the celestial river—
distressed by the rounds of worldly existence, crying aloud '<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>'—
when shall we reach that state overwhelmed with copious tears welling up from within? || BharSt_3.85 ||

children.text: mahādevo devaḥ sarid api ca saiṣā sura-saridguhā
children.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s> is the God; the river is none other than this celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: evāgāraṃ vasanam api tā eva haritaḥ |
children.translated_text: a cave is the dwelling; the garments are these very tree-barks.

children.text: suhṛdā kālo 'yaṃ vratm idam adainya-vratam idaṃ
children.translated_text: Time itself is the friend; this vow is the vow free from wretchedness—

children.text: kiyad vā vakṣyāmo vaṭa-viṭapa evāstu dayitā || BharSt_3.- ||
children.translated_text: how much more shall we say? Let the banyan tree itself be the beloved. || BharSt_3.- ||
Having given away all possessions, with hearts full of tender compassion,
remembering the ill-fated course of destiny in this world of <s>saṃsāra</s>—
we shall spend the nights in a sacred forest, bathed in the rays of the full autumn moon,
with meditation on the feet of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) as our sole refuge. || BharSt_3.86 ||
When, dwelling in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> on the bank of the celestial river,
wearing only a loincloth, placing cupped hands upon my head,
crying out 'O Lord of <s>Gaurī</s>, O Destroyer of the Triple City, O <s>Śambhu</s>, O Three-eyed One,

children.text: prasīdetyākrośan nimiṣam iva neṣyāmi divasān || BharSt_3.87 ||
children.translated_text: be gracious!'—shall I pass my days as if they were but moments? || BharSt_3.87 ||
In the gardens there, various modes of eating become the most intense austerity;
a loincloth becomes the finest garment; wandering for alms becomes adornment;

children.text: āsannaṃ maraṇaṃ ca maṅgala-samaṃ yasyāṃ samutpadyate
children.translated_text: and approaching death becomes auspicious—in that <s>Kāśī</s> where such transformation arises,

children.text: tāṃ kāśīṃ parihṛtya hanta vibudhair anyatra kiṃ sthīyate || BharSt_3.- ||
children.translated_text: alas, why would the wise dwell elsewhere, having abandoned her? || BharSt_3.- ||

children.text: snātvā gāṅgaiḥ payobhiḥ śuci-kusuma-phalair arcayitvā vibho tvā
children.translated_text: Having bathed in the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having worshipped You, O Lord, with pure flowers and fruits,
having fixed my meditation on the object of contemplation, at the foot of a stone couch in a mountain cave—
delighting in the Self, eating only fruits, devoted to the teacher's words—O Enemy of <s>Smara</s> (Kāma), by Your grace,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ mokṣye kadāhaṃ sama-kara-caraṇe puṃsi sevāsamuttham || BharSt_3.88 ||
children.translated_text: when shall I be freed from the suffering born of servitude, O Being of even hands and feet? || BharSt_3.88 ||
Alone, desireless, at peace, with my hand as my bowl, sky-clad—
when, O <s>Śambhu</s>, shall I become capable of uprooting all <s>karma</s>? || BharSt_3.89 ||
Let the hand be made a vessel; let one be content with alms that are naturally pure;

children.text: yatra kvāpi niṣīdatāṃ bahu-tṛṇaṃ viśvaṃ muhuḥ paśyatām |
children.translated_text: let one sit down anywhere—the world has abundant grass; let one gaze upon the world repeatedly—
even without abandoning the body, some ineffable sweetness, touching the realization of unbroken supreme bliss,

children.text: madhvā ko 'pi śiva-prasāda-sulabhaḥ sampatsyate yoginām || BharSt_3.90 ||
children.translated_text: easily attained by the grace of <s>Śiva</s>, shall come to the <s>yogins</s>. || BharSt_3.90 ||
A loincloth tattered into a hundred pieces; a patched cloak likewise;

children.text: naiścintyaṃ nirapekṣa-bhaikṣyam aśanaṃ nidrā śmaśāne vane |
children.translated_text: carefree eating of alms without expectation; sleep in the cremation ground or the forest;

children.text: svātantryeṇa niraṅkuśaṃ viharaṇaṃ svāntaṃ praśāntaṃ sadā
children.translated_text: wandering freely without restraint; the inner self always at peace;

children.text: sthairyaṃ yoga-mahotsave 'pi ca yadi trailokya-rājyena kim || BharSt_3.91 ||
children.translated_text: and steadfastness even in the great festival of <s>yoga</s>—if one has these, what need is there of sovereignty over the three worlds? || BharSt_3.91 ||
The universe (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) is a mere sphere—what greed could it inspire in the high-minded?

children.text: śapharī-sphurtenābdhiḥ kṣubdho na khalu jāyate || BharSt_3.92 ||
children.translated_text: The ocean is surely not disturbed by the splashing of a small fish. || BharSt_3.92 ||

children.text: mātar lakṣmi bhajasva kañcid aparaṃ mat-kāṅkṣiṇī mā sma bhūr
children.translated_text: O Mother <s>Lakṣmī</s>, worship someone else! Do not set your hopes on me;

children.text: bhogeṣu spṛhayālavas tava vaśe kā niḥspṛhāṇām asi |
children.translated_text: those who crave pleasures are in your power—what are you to those who are desireless?
Now we seek our livelihood with alms alone,

children.text: bhikṣā-vastubhir eva samprati vayaṃ vṛttiṃ samīhāmahe || BharSt_3.93 ||
children.translated_text: in vessels made of freshly-stitched <s>palāśa</s> leaf-cups, purified by nature. || BharSt_3.93 ||
The earth is the great bed; the creeper-like arms are the ample pillow;
the sky is the canopy; this favorable breeze is the fan;
the autumn moon is the lamp—delighting in the company of the lady Renunciation,

children.text: sukhī śāntaḥ śete munir atanu-bhūtir nṛpa iva || BharSt_3.94 ||
children.translated_text: the sage sleeps happily, at peace, his glory no less than a king's. || BharSt_3.94 ||
Eating alms, free from association with the crowd, always self-directed in action,
devoted to the path of detachment from gain and loss—such an ascetic stands firm.
Wearing tattered garments scattered on the road, seated on a patched cloth,
free from pride and ego, his sole desire fixed on the enjoyment of the bliss of tranquility. || BharSt_3.95 ||

children.text: caṇḍālaḥ kim ayaṃ dvijātir athavā śūdro 'tha kiṃ tāpasaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Is this a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>? A twice-born? Or a <s>Śūdra</s>? Or an ascetic?

children.text: kiṃ vā tattva-viveka-peśala-matir yogīśvaraḥ ko 'pi kim |
children.translated_text: Or is he some master <s>yogin</s> with a mind skilled in discerning the truth?'—
addressed on the road by people chattering with such speculative talk,

children.text: na kruddhāḥ pathi naiva tuṣṭa-manaso yānti svayaṃ yoginaḥ || BharSt_3.96 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>yogins</s> go on their way, neither angered nor pleased in mind. || BharSt_3.96 ||
Food free from violence, obtained without effort—ordained by the Creator as wind;
the animals, eating grass-sprouts, are content, sleeping on the ground.
Such is the livelihood made for those whose minds are capable of crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>—

children.text: tām anveṣayatāṃ prayānti satataṃ sarvaṃ samāptiṃ guṇāḥ || BharSt_3.97 ||
children.translated_text: for those who seek that livelihood, all virtues constantly come to perfection. || BharSt_3.97 ||
On the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, seated in <s>padmāsana</s> (lotus-posture) upon a Himalayan rock,
having entered <s>yoga-nidrā</s> (yogic sleep) through the practice of meditation on <s>Brahman</s>—

children.text: kiṃ tair bhāvyaṃ mama sudivasair yatra te nirviśaṅkāḥ
children.translated_text: will those blessed days come for me, when fearless

children.text: kaṇḍūyante jaraṭha-hariṇāḥ svāṅgam aṅge madīye || BharSt_3.98 ||
children.translated_text: old deer scratch their bodies against my limbs? || BharSt_3.98 ||

children.text: jīrṇāḥ kanthā tataḥ kiṃ sitam amala-paṭaṃ paṭṭa-sūtraṃ tataḥ kiṃ
children.translated_text: A worn-out patched garment—what of it? A white, spotless cloth of silk—what of it?

children.text: ekā bhāryā tataḥ kiṃ haya-kari-sugaṇair āvṛto vā tataḥ kim |
children.translated_text: One wife—what of it? Surrounded by troops of horses and elephants—what of it?

children.text: bhaktaṃ bhuktaṃ tataḥ kiṃ kadaśanam athavā vāsarānte tataḥ kiṃ
children.translated_text: A full meal eaten—what of it? Or poor food at the end of the day—what of it?

children.text: vyakta-jyotir na vāntarmathita-bhava-bhayaṃ vaibhavaṃ vā tataḥ kim || BharSt_3.- ||
children.translated_text: If the inner light is manifest and the fear of worldly existence is churned away—what then of any wealth? || BharSt_3.- ||

children.text: pāṇiḥ pātraṃ pavitraṃ bhramaṇa-parigataṃ bhaikṣyam akṣayyam annaṃ
children.translated_text: The hand is the pure vessel; alms obtained through wandering are the inexhaustible food;

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ vastram āśā-daśakam acapalaṃ talpam asvalpam urvīm |
children.translated_text: the ten directions are the vast garment; the earth, no small thing, is the steady bed.
Those whose inner contentment has matured through the embodiment of non-attachment,
those blessed ones who have cast off the mass of miserable entanglements, uproot all <s>karma</s>. || BharSt_3.99 ||
Under that great teaching in which even sovereignty over the three worlds is tasteless—

children.text: tal labdhvāsana-vastra-māna-ghaṭane bhoge ratiṃ mā kṛthāḥ |
children.translated_text: having attained it, do not take delight in the enjoyment of arranging seats, garments, and honors.

children.text: bhogaḥ ko 'pi sa eka eva paramo nityoditā jṛmbhane
children.translated_text: There is one supreme enjoyment, ever arising in its unfolding,

children.text: yat-svādād virasā bhavanti visayās trailokya-rājyādayaḥ || BharSt_3.99*1 ||
children.translated_text: by the taste of which sense-objects, sovereignty over the three worlds and the like, become insipid. || BharSt_3.99*1 ||

children.text: mātar medini tāta māruti sakhe tejaḥ subandho jala
children.translated_text: O Mother Earth, O Father Wind, O Friend Fire, O Dear Kinsman Water,

children.text: bhrātar vyoma nibaddha eṣa bhavatām antyaḥ praṇāmāñjaliḥ |
children.translated_text: O Brother Sky—here is my final salutation with joined palms to you all.
Through the merit born from association with you, I have gained the glory of pure knowledge, brilliantly shining forth,
which has dispelled all delusion—and now I am dissolved in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. || BharSt_3.100 ||

children.text: śayyā śaila-śilā-gṛhaṃ giri-guhā vastraṃ taruṇāṃ tvacaḥ
children.translated_text: The bed is a mountain rock; the house a mountain cave; the garment the bark of trees;

children.text: sāraṅgāḥ suhṛdo nanu kṣiti-ruhāṃ vṛttiḥ phalaiḥ komalaiḥ |
children.translated_text: deer are their friends; surely the livelihood of trees is provided by soft fruits.

children.text: yesāṃ nirjharam ambu-pānam ucitaṃ ratyai tu vidyāṅganā
children.translated_text: Their fitting drink is waterfall water; and for love, the lady of Knowledge—

children.text: manye te parameśvarāḥ śirasi yari baddho na sevāñjaliḥ || BharSt_3.100*1 ||
children.translated_text: I consider them supreme lords, those who have not bound upon their heads the salutation of servitude. || BharSt_3.100*1 ||

children.text: dhairyaṃ yasya pitā kṣamā ca jananī śāntiś ciraṃ gehinī
children.translated_text: He whose father is Courage, whose mother is Forbearance, whose eternal wife is Peace,

children.text: satyaṃ mitram idaṃ dayā ca bhaginī bhrātā manaḥ-saṃyamaḥ |
children.translated_text: whose friend is Truth, whose sister is Compassion, whose brother is Self-control,

children.text: śayyā bhūmi-talaṃ diśo 'pi vasanaṃ jñānāmṛtaṃ bhojanaṃ
children.translated_text: whose bed is the surface of the earth, whose garment is the directions, whose food is the nectar of Knowledge—

children.text: hy ete yasya kuṭumbino vada sakhe kasmād bhayaṃ yoginaḥ || BharSt_3.100*2 ||
children.translated_text: tell me, O friend, of what should such a <s>yogin</s> be afraid, whose household members are these? || BharSt_3.100*2 ||

children.text: aho vā hāre vā balavati ripau vā suhṛdi vā
children.translated_text: Whether in gain or in loss, with a powerful enemy or a friend,

children.text: maṇau vā loṣṭhe vā kusuma-śayane vā dṛṣadi vā |
children.translated_text: with a jewel or a clod of earth, on a bed of flowers or on stone,

children.text: tṛṇe vā straiṇe vā mama sama-dṛśo yānti divasāḥ
children.translated_text: with a blade of grass or with a woman—my days pass in equanimity,

children.text: kvacit puṇyāraṇye śiva śiva śiveti pralapataḥ || BharSt_3.100*3 ||
children.translated_text: somewhere in a sacred forest, murmuring '<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>.' || BharSt_3.100*3 ||
